• 2 tbsp almond meal  
• 1 tbsp carob powder  

Method:  
1. Chill carrot ribbons on ice.  
2. Whisk kefir, rosewater and salt; use a dropper to place tiny pearls atop the carrots.  
3. Toast almond meal until golden, stir in carob powder and cool.  
4. Sprinkle carob-almond soil over the carpaccio and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Jasmine‐Honey Foam with Charred Red Pepper Broth and Millet‐Stuffed Sweet Potato Leaf Dumplings  
Ingredients:
- 12 sweet potato leaves, blanched  
- ½ cup cooked millet  
- 1 tbsp grated fresh ginger  
- 1 tsp soy sauce  
- 2 red bell peppers, charred, peeled and chopped  
- 300 ml vegetable broth  
- 100 ml water  
- 1 tbsp honey  
- ½ tsp jasmine tea leaves  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Mix millet, ginger, soy sauce and a pinch of salt. Place 1 tsp filling on each leaf, fold into dumplings.  
2. Simmer peppers with broth and water 10 min, purée, season and keep warm.  
3. Steep jasmine leaves in 50 ml warm water with honey 5 min, strain, stir in lecithin and blend into foam.  
4. Poach dumplings in gently simmering water 3 min, drain.  
5. Arrange dumplings in shallow bowls, ladle in red pepper broth, and top each with a spoonful of jasmine-honey foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Roasted Jackfruit Seed Crisps with Orange-Blossom Gel and Lemongrass-Smoke Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 cup jackfruit seeds, cleaned and patted dry  
• 100 ml orange-blossom water  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml light vegetable stock  
• 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine salt  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 180 °C. Arrange seeds on a baking sheet, roast 20 min until golden-crisp; cool.  
2. In a small saucepan, bring orange-blossom water and agar to a simmer, stir 1 min until dissolved, pour into a thin layer, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Smoke bruised lemongrass briefly over hot charcoal or in a smoking gun, then steep in warm vegetable stock for 10 min; strain, season with salt, whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve, scatter jackfruit seed crisps on a chilled plate, dot with orange-blossom gel cubes, crown with a spoonful of lemongrass-smoke foam and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Roasted Quince Carpaccio with Silken-Tofu Cloud, Goji-Berry Purée & Black-Sesame Dust

Ingredients:
• 1 small quince, peeled, cored, thinly sliced  
• 25 g silken tofu  
• 20 g dried goji berries  
• 1 tsp sugar  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 2 tsp black sesame seeds, toasted  
• pinch fine sea salt

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 140 °C. Arrange quince slices on a parchment-lined tray, roast 12–15 min until just tender; cool.  
2. Soak goji berries in 20 ml warm water for 10 min, purée with sugar, strain and reserve.  
3. Blend silken tofu, lecithin and a pinch of salt with an immersion blender until light and airy.  
4. Grind 1 tsp sesame seeds to a fine powder; reserve the other 1 tsp whole.  
5. To serve, fan quince carpaccio on chilled plates, drizzle with goji-berry purée, dollop silken-tofu cloud, and sprinkle with black-sesame dust and whole seeds. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Lotus Seed Loops with Tarragon-Cream Foam and Beetroot Dust  
Ingredients: 30 g dried lotus seeds; pinch fine salt; 50 ml heavy cream; 1 sprig fresh tarragon; ½ tsp soy lecithin; 1 tsp beetroot powder.  
Method: Toast lotus seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat until they “pop” and turn golden; season with salt. Warm cream with tarragon sprig, steep 10 min, strain and discard herbs. Whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to create a stable foam. Dust chilled plates with beetroot powder, arrange lotus seed loops, top each with a dollop of tarragon-cream foam, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Grape-Leaf–Wrapped Honeydew-Ricotta Dumplings with Rosemary-Olive Foam

Ingredients:
• 8 fresh grape leaves, stems trimmed  
• 100 g ricotta  
• ½ cup diced honeydew melon  
• Zest of 1 lemon  
• Pinch fine salt  
• 1 sprig fresh rosemary  
• 50 ml extra-virgin olive oil  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Neutral oil for searing  

Method:
1. Combine ricotta, honeydew, lemon zest and salt.  
2. Place 1 Tbsp filling on each leaf, fold into small parcels.  
3. Heat neutral oil in a skillet over medium; sear parcels until grape leaves are lightly charred, about 1 min per side.  
4. Gently warm olive oil with rosemary for 5 min, let cool, discard rosemary, then whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam.  
5. Plate dumplings and spoon rosemary-olive foam on top. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Szechuan Peppercorn–Poached Chayote Ribbon Cups with Lemongrass–Coconut Snow and Charcoal Basil Dust

Ingredients:
• 1 medium chayote, peeled  
• 5 g Szechuan peppercorns  
• 200 ml water  
• 1 tbsp sugar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised  
• 1 egg white  
• 1 fresh basil leaf  
• ¼ tsp activated charcoal powder  
• Pinch of fine sea salt  

Method:
1. In a small pot, simmer water, peppercorns and sugar for 5 min. Strain, return to a gentle simmer. Slice chayote into 2 mm ribbons and blanch 1 min until pliable. Shock in ice water, drain, and form each ribbon into a little “cup.”  
2. Warm coconut milk with bruised lemongrass just below a simmer, remove lemongrass, pour into a shallow tray and freeze until solid (≈2 hr). Grate into fluffy “snow.”  
3. Char basil leaf directly over a flame until crisp, grind to a fine powder and blend with charcoal powder to make a dark dust.  
4. Whip egg white with a pinch of salt to soft peaks; use immediately to support snow in cups.  
5. To serve, place 3 chayote cups per plate, fill each with lemongrass–coconut snow topped by a tuft of whipped egg white, then sift charcoal basil dust over them.

Recipe Title: Blue Corn Tapioca Crisp with Blackcurrant-Lime Gelee and Smoked Cucumber Mist  
Ingredients:  
• ½ cup blue cornmeal  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• pinch of salt  
• 100 ml blackcurrant juice  
• zest and juice of 1 lime  
• 1 g gelatin  
• 1 small cucumber, peeled  
• 1 tsp hickory-smoked salt  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Whisk cornmeal, tapioca, salt and just enough water into a thin batter. Spread 2 mm on a silicone mat; bake at 140 °C until crisp (≈15 min).  
2. Warm blackcurrant juice with lime zest and juice. Soften gelatin in cold water, stir in until dissolved. Chill in a thin layer until set; cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Purée cucumber with smoked salt and lecithin; aerate briefly with an immersion blender to form a light mist.  
4. On a chilled plate, place one blue-corn crisp, scatter blackcurrant-lime gelee cubes atop, and lightly cloud with cucumber mist. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Artichoke Leaf Lace with Kalamansi-Coconut Gel and Pink Peppercorn Mist  
Ingredients:
• 8 large artichoke leaves, patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• 1 tsp agar-agar  
• 3 Tbsp kalamansi (or lime) juice  
• 1 tsp sugar  
• ½ tsp crushed pink peppercorns  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly dust each artichoke leaf in tapioca starch and fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain and cool.  
2. Warm coconut milk with sugar; whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill and cut into cubes.  
3. Blend crushed peppercorns with lecithin and 30 ml water; aerate into a fine mist.  
4. Arrange leaf laces on chilled plates, scatter coconut-kalamansi gel cubes, and finish by lightly clouding with pink peppercorn mist.

Recipe Title: Candied Kale‐Stem Laces with Mango–Jalapeño Gel and Kaffir‐Lime–Basil Mist  
Ingredients:
- 6 kale stems, peeled into thin ribbons  
- 50 g sugar + 50 ml water  
- 1 ripe mango, puréed  
- 1 small jalapeño, seeded and minced  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 5 kaffir-lime leaves  
- 5 fresh basil leaves  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Pinch of fine salt  

Method:
1. Bring sugar and water to a simmer, add kale ribbons and poach 2 min. Remove, pat dry and dehydrate at 60 °C until crisp.  
2. Simmer mango purée with jalapeño and a pinch of salt 5 min. Whisk in agar-agar, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Steep kaffir-lime leaves and basil in 30 ml hot water 10 min, strain, stir in lecithin and blend into a fine mist.  
4. To serve, arrange candied kale-stem laces on a chilled plate, scatter mango–jalapeño gel cubes atop, and lightly cloud with kaffir-lime–basil mist. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura Pumpkin-Leaf Petal Cups with Kumquat-Ginger Gel and Clover-Honey Vapor

Ingredients:
- 8 outer pumpkin leaves (young, tender)
- ½ cup rice flour
- ¼ cup cornstarch
- Pinch fine salt
- 1 cup ice-cold sparkling water
- Zest and juice of 4 kumquats
- 1 g agar-agar
- 2 Tbsp honey (clover or wildflower)
- ½ tsp fresh-grated ginger
- ½ tsp soy lecithin
- Neutral oil for frying

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour, cornstarch, salt and sparkling water to a smooth, thin batter. Pat leaves dry, dip lightly and deep-fry at 180 °C until crisp “cups.” Drain on paper.
2. Simmer kumquat juice, zest and ginger with agar-agar for 2 min; pour into a shallow tray, chill until set, then cut into small gel cubes.
3. Warm honey with 1 Tbsp water (no simmer), stir in lecithin and whip briefly to create a light vapor.
4. Assemble by nestling kumquat-ginger gel in each pumpkin-leaf cup and enveloping the plate in a wispy clover-honey vapor. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Water Lily Petal Lace with Tamarind-Jicama Gel and Smoked Black Salt-Coconut Foam

Ingredients:
- 12 edible water lily petals, patted dry  
- 100 ml tamarind concentrate  
- 50 g jicama purée  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 50 ml coconut milk  
- ½ tsp fenugreek powder  
- ½ tsp smoked black salt  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly char petals over a gas flame until edges crisp; cool.  
2. In a saucepan, warm tamarind concentrate with jicama purée; whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min; pour into a thin tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with fenugreek and smoked black salt; cool slightly, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. On chilled plates, fan charred petals into lace shapes, scatter tamarind-jicama gel cubes, and crown with a spoonful of smoked black salt-coconut foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Pickled Watermelon Rind Spirals with Matcha-Kaffir Lime Foam and Black Sesame Soil

Ingredients:
• 200 g white watermelon rind (peeled)  
• 50 ml rice vinegar  
• 1 tbsp sugar  
• ¼ tsp sea salt  
• Zest and juice of 1 kaffir lime  
• ½ tsp matcha powder  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 1 tbsp black sesame seeds  

Method:
1. Slice rind into 3 mm ribbons, blanch 30 s, shock in ice.  
2. Warm vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved; cool, submerge ribbons 2 hrs, then coil into spirals.  
3. Mix lime juice, zest and matcha; whisk in lecithin with immersion blender to form foam.  
4. Toast sesame seeds until fragrant, grind coarsely.  
5. Arrange spirals on plate, top with matcha-lime foam, and dust with black sesame soil.

Recipe Title: Saffron-Camel-Milk Panna Cotta with Pistachio-Basil Soil and Rosewater-Lavender Caviar

Ingredients:
– 150 ml camel milk  
– 50 ml heavy cream  
– 3 saffron threads  
– 1 tbsp sugar  
– 2 tsp powdered gelatin  
– 3 tbsp finely ground pistachios  
– ½ tsp dried basil, ground  
– 50 ml rosewater  
– 1 tbsp dried culinary lavender  
– 1 tsp agar-agar  
– Neutral oil (for caviar)

Method:
1. Soften gelatin in 2 tbsp cold water. Heat camel milk, cream, saffron and sugar to a simmer, whisk in gelatin until dissolved, strain and pour into small molds. Chill until set (≈3 hr).  
2. Combine pistachios and basil powder on a plate for “soil.”  
3. Steep lavender in warm rosewater 10 min, strain, return to a gentle simmer with agar-agar until dissolved. Using a dropper, drip the warm liquid into chilled neutral oil to form firm “caviar,” then rinse under cold water.  
4. Unmold panna cotta onto chilled plates, dust with pistachio-basil soil and scatter rosewater-lavender caviar on top. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Starfruit Cups with Passionfruit-Chia Gel and Coconut-Kaffir Lime Foam

Ingredients:
• 2 ripe starfruits  
• 100 ml passionfruit juice  
• 1 Tbsp chia seeds  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• Zest of 1 kaffir lime  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch of fine salt  

Method:
1. Slice starfruit crosswise into 5 mm “stars,” scoop a small cavity in each to form cups.  
2. Stir chia into passionfruit juice, let sit 30 min until thickened.  
3. Warm coconut milk with lime zest and salt, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. Spoon passionfruit-chia gel into each starfruit cup and top with a dollop of coconut-kaffir lime foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Chai-Spiced Socca Crisp with Rose-Petal Marmalade and Basil-Lime Foam

Ingredients:
• ½ cup chickpea flour  
• ½ tsp ground cinnamon, cardamom, ginger (each)  
• Pinch fine salt  
• ¾ cup cold water  
• 1 tbsp olive oil (+ extra for pan)  
• 3 tbsp rose-petal jam  
• ¼ cup fresh basil leaves  
• Zest and juice of ½ lime  
• ¼ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Whisk chickpea flour, spices, salt, water and 1 tbsp oil until smooth; rest 15 min.  
2. Preheat oven to 200 °C. Lightly oil a rimmed baking sheet, pour batter in a thin layer, bake until lacy and crisp (≈12 min). Cool.  
3. Spread rose-petal jam over each crisp.  
4. Blend basil, lime zest, juice and lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
5. Serve crisps on plates, crown with basil-lime foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Grape–Tendril Lace with Earl Grey Snow and Honey-Tarragon Foam

Ingredients:
• 12 fresh grape tendrils (washed)  
• 100 ml water  
• 1 tbsp sugar  
• 1 Earl Grey tea bag  
• 1 tbsp honey  
• 1 sprig fresh tarragon  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 1 egg white  
• Pinch fine salt  

Method:
1. Blanch tendrils 30 s in boiling water, pat dry, then char over a gas flame or in a skillet until crisp.  
2. Simmer water, sugar and tea bag 5 min; strain, cool, freeze in a shallow tray, and scrape into “snow.”  
3. Warm honey with tarragon 5 min; remove herb, cool, whisk in lecithin to form a light foam.  
4. Whip egg white with salt to soft peaks and gently fold in half the honey-tarragon foam.  
5. On chilled plates, lay tendril laces, sprinkle Earl Grey snow atop, and crown each with a dollop of egg-white–foam and a swirl of honey-tarragon foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Radish-Leaf Lace with Rhubarb-Vanilla Snow and Horseradish-Lemongrass Mist

Ingredients:
• 8 large radish leaves, patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 g rhubarb, chopped  
• 1 Tbsp sugar  
• Seeds of ½ vanilla bean  
• 1 tsp freshly grated horseradish  
• 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust leaves with starch and deep-fry at 170 °C until crisp; drain on paper.  
2. Simmer rhubarb, sugar and vanilla seeds 8 min, cool, freeze in a shallow tray, then grate into “snow.”  
3. Steep horseradish and lemongrass in 50 ml hot water 5 min, strain, cool, whisk in lecithin to create a fine mist.  
4. On chilled plates, place one leaf lace, mound rhubarb-vanilla snow atop, and veil with horseradish-lemongrass mist.

Recipe Title: Roasted Kabocha-Seed Brittle with Green Apple–Pandan Gel and Lemon-Verbena Foam

Ingredients:
- 1 cup kabocha pumpkin seeds, rinsed, patted dry
- ½ cup granulated sugar
- 1 tbsp unsalted butter
- 100 ml green apple juice
- 1 g agar-agar
- 1 tsp pandan extract
- 50 ml lemon-verbena infusion (steep 2 tbsp fresh verbena leaves in 50 ml hot water, then strain)
- ½ tsp soy lecithin
- pinch fine sea salt

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 180 °C. Toss seeds with salt, roast 12 min until golden; cool.
2. In a saucepan, melt sugar over medium until amber. Remove from heat, whisk in butter until smooth, stir in half the seeds, then pour onto parchment. Cool and break into shards.
3. Combine apple juice, pandan and agar-agar in a small pot; simmer 1 min. Pour into a thin layer, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.
4. Whisk lemon-verbena infusion with lecithin using an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.
5. To serve, scatter brittle shards on a chilled plate, nestle gel cubes among them, and spoon dollops of lemon-verbena foam on top.

Recipe Title: Fermented Bamboo-Shoot Spirals with Turmeric-Lime Coconut Foam and Toasted Pine-Nut Soil

Ingredients:
• 1 young bamboo shoot, peeled and thinly sliced into 3 mm ribbons  
• 1 Tbsp sea salt  
• ½ tsp sugar  
• 200 ml water  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• ½ tsp ground turmeric  
• Zest and juice of 1 lime  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 30 g pine nuts

Method:
1. Toss bamboo ribbons with salt and sugar, submerge in water, cover loosely and ferment at 20 °C for 24 hr. Rinse, pat dry and coil into spirals.  
2. Warm coconut milk with turmeric and lime zest until just below simmer, remove from heat, stir in lime juice and lecithin, then blend to a stable foam.  
3. Toast pine nuts until golden, cool and grind coarsely into “soil.”  
4. Arrange bamboo spirals on chilled plates, spoon turmeric-lime foam over them, and finish with a dusting of pine-nut soil. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Roasted Salsify Ribbons with Lapsang Souchong Caviar and Chervil-Lime Foam

Ingredients:
• 2 medium salsify roots, peeled and sliced into 2 mm ribbons  
• 100 ml strong Lapsang Souchong tea  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• Neutral oil (4 °C, for caviar)  
• 20 ml chopped fresh chervil  
• Zest and juice of 1 lime  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Sea salt  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 200 °C. Toss salsify ribbons with oil and salt; roast until tender-crispy, ~12 min.  
2. Simmer tea with agar-agar 2 min, strain. While warm, drop by the teaspoon into chilled oil to form caviar; rinse and drain.  
3. Blend chervil, lime juice, zest and lecithin with an immersion blender into a fine foam.  
4. Arrange salsify ribbons on a chilled plate, scatter tea caviar over them and crown with chervil-lime foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Stinging Nettle Tips with Elderflower-Mead Glaze and Lemon Balm Foam

Ingredients:
• 20 fresh stinging nettle tips, blanched 30 s and shocked  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Pinch fine salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 2 Tbsp elderflower cordial  
• 1 Tbsp mead (or light honey)  
• 1 tsp lemon juice  
• 50 ml lemon balm infusion (steep 5 g leaves in 50 ml water, cool)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a thin batter; keep cold.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip nettle tips in batter, fry 1–2 min until crisp, drain.  
3. In a small pan, simmer elderflower cordial, mead and lemon juice until syrupy; brush over hot nettles.  
4. Whisk lemon balm infusion with lecithin using an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
5. Arrange nettles on a plate, crown with a dollop of lemon balm foam and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Roasted Okra Pod Chips with Blueberry-Mint Gelée and Smoked Thyme Soil

Ingredients:
- 12 fresh okra pods, sliced 2 mm thick  
- 100 ml blueberry juice  
- 1 tsp sugar  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 10 mint leaves  
- Pinch fine salt  
- 2 sprigs thyme  
- ½ tsp smoked salt  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 180 °C. Toss okra slices with oil and salt; roast 12–15 min until crisp. Cool on paper.  
2. Bring blueberry juice, sugar and mint to a gentle simmer, steep 3 min, strain, return to heat, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour thinly into a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. In a dry skillet char thyme leaves until brittle; cool and grind with smoked salt into a coarse “soil.”  
4. Arrange okra chips on chilled plates, scatter gelée cubes atop, and dust with thyme soil. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Roasted Sprouted Buckwheat Crisps with Elderberry Gelée and Marigold-Petal Foam

Ingredients:
- 100 g buckwheat groats, soaked 8 hr and sprouted 48 hr  
- 1 tbsp neutral oil  
- fine sea salt  
- 120 ml elderberry juice  
- 1 tsp sugar  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 2 tbsp dried marigold petals  
- 50 ml water  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 160 °C. Drain sprouts, toss with oil and a pinch of salt, spread thin on a baking sheet, roast 12–15 min until crisp; cool.  
2. In a saucepan warm elderberry juice with sugar, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a shallow tray, chill until set (~30 min), then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Steep marigold petals in 50 ml hot water 5 min, strain, stir in lecithin and aerate with an immersion blender into a light foam.  
4. To serve, arrange buckwheat crisps on chilled plates, scatter elderberry gelée cubes over them and crown with dollops of marigold-petal foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Eggplant Lace with Prickly Pear–Black Pepper Gel and Wood Sorrel Foam
Ingredients:
- 1 small eggplant, peeled into 2 mm ribbons  
- 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral frying oil  
- 100 ml prickly pear juice  
- 1 tsp crushed black peppercorns  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 50 ml wood sorrel infusion (5 g leaves steeped in 50 ml hot water)  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Dust eggplant ribbons lightly in tapioca starch. Fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain on paper and cool.  
2. Simmer prickly pear juice with peppercorns for 2 min; strain, return to heat, whisk in agar-agar, pour into a shallow tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Strain wood sorrel infusion, cool, stir in lecithin and aerate with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. Fan eggplant laces on a chilled plate, scatter gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of wood sorrel foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Hijiki Lace with Yuzu-Apple Snow and Ginger-Scallion Foam  
Ingredients: 5 g dried hijiki; neutral oil; 100 ml apple juice; 1 Tbsp yuzu juice; 1 g agar-agar; 50 ml water; 10 g sliced scallion; 1 tsp grated ginger; ½ tsp soy lecithin; pinch salt.  
Method:  
1. Heat oil to 170 °C, fry hijiki in small bundles until lace-crisp; drain on paper.  
2. Simmer apple juice, yuzu and agar-agar 1 min, spread thin, chill, freeze and grate into snow.  
3. Simmer water, scallion and ginger 5 min, strain, cool and whisk in lecithin into a stable foam.  
4. On chilled plates, lay hijiki lace, sprinkle yuzu-apple snow, and crown with ginger-scallion foam.

Recipe Title: Daylily-Bud Confit with Lemon-Verbena Foam and Hazelnut Sand

Ingredients:
• 20 fresh daylily buds, trimmed  
• 3 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil  
• 1 tsp honey  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• Zest and juice of ½ lemon  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 2 sprigs fresh lemon-verbena  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 2 Tbsp toasted hazelnut meal  

Method:
1. In a small skillet over low heat, warm olive oil, honey and salt. Add daylily buds and poach gently 5 min. Drain.  
2. Warm cream with verbena sprigs, steep 5 min, strain; whisk in lecithin until foamy.  
3. On chilled plates, sprinkle hazelnut meal, arrange confit buds, zest with lemon, dot with lemon juice and crown with verbena foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Carrot-Top Lace with Cherry-Schisandra Gel and Dill Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 1 cup carrot tops, washed  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Pinch fine salt  
• 100 ml cherry juice  
• 1 Tbsp dried schisandra berries  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml water  
• handful fresh dill  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Purée carrot tops with starch, salt and 1 Tbsp oil until smooth; spread ultra-thin on a silicone mat and bake at 150 °C for 12 min until lace-like; cool.  
2. Simmer cherry juice with schisandra for 3 min, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved; pour into a thin layer, chill 30 min, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Steep dill in warm water for 5 min, strain, stir in lecithin and blend into a stable foam.  
4. On a chilled plate, arrange carrot-top lace, scatter cherry-schisandra gel cubes and crown with dill foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Lotus Stem Lace with Pink Pepper–Peach Gel and Lemongrass–Coconut Snow  
Ingredients:
• 1 fresh lotus stem, peeled and thinly sliced  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil (for frying)  
• 100 g ripe peach purée  
• 1 tsp crushed pink peppercorns  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised  

Method:
1. Dust lotus slices in tapioca starch; fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp. Drain.  
2. Simmer peach purée with pink peppercorns 2 min, strain, whisk in agar-agar, pour thin in a tray and chill until firm; cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with lemongrass, steep 5 min, discard lemongrass, freeze into a block, then grate into “snow.”  
4. Fan lotus lace on chilled plates, scatter peach gel cubes, crown with lemongrass–coconut snow, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Puffed Amaranth Cup with Smoked Urfa Pepper Labneh & Kumquat–Yerba Mate Vapor

Ingredients:
• 50 g amaranth  
• neutral oil for puffing  
• 100 g labneh  
• ½ tsp Urfa biber (smoked pepper)  
• pinch fine sea salt  
• 2 kumquats (juice + zest)  
• 100 ml strong yerba mate infusion, cooled  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Heat 1 cm oil in a deep skillet to 180 °C. Sprinkle in amaranth, cover and let pop 20–30 s. Drain on paper, then press warm puffs into 3 small cup shapes.  
2. Stir Urfa biber and salt into labneh; pipe a quenelle into each amaranth cup.  
3. Whisk yerba mate infusion, kumquat juice and zest with lecithin; aerate with an immersion blender into a fine vapor.  
4. Arrange cups on chilled plates, cloud them with kumquat–yerba mate vapor, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Birch-Sap Gelee with Violet-Petal Ribbons and Roasted Chestnut Sand  
Ingredients:
- 120 ml fresh birch sap  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 1 tsp sugar  
- pinch fine sea salt  
- a handful edible violet petals  
- 50 g roasted chestnuts, finely ground  

Method:
1. Warm birch sap with sugar and salt until just below simmer, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved, pour into a shallow tray and chill until firm.  
2. Cut the gelee into small cubes.  
3. Arrange a thin layer of chestnut “sand” on each chilled plate, top with gelee cubes and scatter violet petals among them. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Celery-Leaf Lace with Pomegranate-Mint Gel and Nutmeg-Lime Foam

Ingredients:
• 8 celery leaves, washed and patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 150 ml pomegranate juice  
• 10 fresh mint leaves  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• Zest and juice of 1 lime  
• Pinch ground nutmeg  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly dust celery leaves in tapioca starch and fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain on paper.  
2. Simmer pomegranate juice, mint and agar-agar 2 min; strain, pour into a thin layer, chill until firm, then cut into small cubes.  
3. Warm cream with lime zest, juice and nutmeg; remove from heat, whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, fan celery-leaf laces on a chilled plate, scatter pomegranate-mint gel cubes over them and crown with a dollop of nutmeg-lime foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Corn-Husk Lace with Polenta-Gel Cubes and Corn-Silk Foam  
Ingredients: outer dried corn husks; tapioca starch; neutral frying oil; ½ cup cornmeal; 1 g agar-agar; 200 ml water; 20 g fresh corn silk; 50 ml heavy cream; ½ tsp soy lecithin; fine sea salt  
Method: 1. Dust husks in tapioca, deep-fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp, drain. 2. Simmer cornmeal in 200 ml water, strain liquid, whisk 100 ml polenta water with agar, simmer 1 min, pour as a thin layer, chill until set, cut into 5 mm cubes. 3. Steep corn silk in 100 ml hot water for 10 min, strain. Warm cream with 50 ml silk infusion, whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam. 4. On chilled plates, fan corn-husk lace, scatter polenta-gel cubes and crown with corn-silk foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Fig-Leaf Lace with Pistachio-Miso Gelee and Anise-Hyssop Foam

Ingredients:
• 6 fresh fig leaves, patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 50 g roasted pistachios, puréed  
• 1 Tbsp white miso  
• 2 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml water, divided  
• 100 ml anise-hyssop infusion (steep 5 g dried leaves in 100 ml hot water, strain)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust fig leaves with tapioca starch and deep-fry at 170 °C until crisp; drain.  
2. In 50 ml water, whisk pistachio purée, miso and salt; bring to a simmer, stir in agar-agar, pour into a thin layer, chill and cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool the anise-hyssop infusion slightly, whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam.  
4. On chilled plates, fan fig-leaf laces, scatter pistachio-miso gelee cubes, and crown with a spoonful of anise-hyssop foam.

Recipe Title: Puffed Quinoa Cups with Strawberry Granita and Chamomile-Basil Foam

Ingredients:
• 50 g quinoa  
• Neutral oil for puffing  
• 200 g strawberries, puréed  
• 1 Tbsp sugar  
• 1 tsp agar-agar  
• 100 ml milk  
• 1 Tbsp dried chamomile flowers  
• 4 basil leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Heat oil to 180 °C, add quinoa to pop (20–30 s), drain and press warm puffs into 3 small cup shapes; cool.  
2. Simmer strawberry purée with sugar 2 min, whisk in agar-agar, pour into a thin layer, chill until firm, then scrape into granita with a fork.  
3. Warm milk with chamomile 5 min, strain, cool, stir in torn basil and lecithin, blend into a stable foam.  
4. Fill each quinoa cup with strawberry granita and crown with chamomile-basil foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Pine-Pollen Rice Tuiles with Rosehip-Cashew Mousse and Freeze-Dried Rhubarb Dust

Ingredients:
• 30 g pine pollen  
• 2 Tbsp rice flour  
• 1 egg white  
• Pinch fine salt  
• 50 g raw cashews (soaked 2 hr, drained)  
• 30 ml rosehip syrup  
• 2 Tbsp heavy cream  
• 20 g freeze-dried rhubarb (powdered)  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 140 °C. Whisk pine pollen, rice flour, egg white and salt to a thin batter.  
2. Spread 1 Tbsp batter as a 5 cm circle on a silicone mat; bake 8–10 min until lacy and golden. Cool to crisp tuiles.  
3. Blend cashews, rosehip syrup and cream until smooth; chill 1 hr to set into a light mousse.  
4. To serve, pipe a small quenelle of mousse onto each tuile and gently dust with freeze-dried rhubarb powder.

Recipe Title: Teff-Lentil Lace with Miso-Blackberry Gel and Lemon-Basil Foam

Ingredients:
• ¼ cup teff flour  
• 2 Tbsp cooked green lentils, puréed  
• Pinch fine salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml blackberry juice  
• 1 tsp white miso  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• Zest and juice of ½ lemon  
• 5 basil leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Whisk teff, lentil purée, salt and just enough water to make a thin batter. Spread ultra-thin on a silicone mat and bake at 150 °C until lace-crisp (≈12 min).  
2. Simmer blackberry juice with miso 2 min, strain, whisk in agar-agar, pour into a shallow tray, chill 30 min, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm cream with lemon zest, cool slightly, stir in lemon juice, torn basil and lecithin; blend to a stable foam.  
4. On each plate, place a piece of teff-lentil lace, scatter miso-blackberry gel cubes atop and crown with a spoonful of lemon-basil foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Roasted Cucumber Blossom Cups with Matcha-Jasmine Gel and Lemongrass-Honeysuckle Foam

Ingredients:
• 6 fresh cucumber blossoms, cleaned  
• 1 Tbsp extra-virgin olive oil  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

• 150 ml strong jasmine tea  
• 1 tsp matcha powder  
• 1 g agar-agar  

• 100 ml lemongrass infusion (steep 1 stalk in 100 ml water)  
• 1 Tbsp honeysuckle syrup  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 180 °C. Lightly brush each blossom with olive oil, place petals on a baking sheet curved inward to form little cups, sprinkle with salt, and roast 8–10 min until crisp.  
2. Warm jasmine tea, whisk in matcha until smooth, add agar-agar, bring to a gentle simmer 1 min, pour in a thin layer on a tray, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool lemongrass infusion, stir in honeysuckle syrup, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. On chilled plates, nestle 3 blossom cups, fill each with matcha-jasmine gel cubes, and top with a spoonful of lemongrass-honeysuckle foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Watercress-Stem Lace with Lychee–Cardamom Gel, Bergamot Foam & Farro Dust

Ingredients:
• 20 g watercress stems, rinsed and patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml lychee juice  
• ½ tsp crushed green cardamom  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml bergamot tea infusion, cooled  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 2 Tbsp farro, toasted and finely ground  
• Pinch fine salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust watercress stems with tapioca starch. Fry in oil at 170 °C until lacy-crispy; drain on paper.  
2. Simmer lychee juice with cardamom for 2 min, strain, whisk in agar-agar, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Stir lecithin into bergamot infusion with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. Grind toasted farro with salt into a coarse “dust.”  
5. To serve, fan watercress laces on chilled plates, scatter lychee–cardamom gel cubes, dust with farro soil, and top with a spoonful of bergamot foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Red Currant Leaf Lace with Carrot-Kefir Gel Cubes and Yarrow-Flower Foam  
Ingredients:
• 8 fresh red currant leaves, patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 g cooked carrot purée  
• 50 ml kefir  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml water  
• 10 g dried yarrow flowers  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust leaves in tapioca starch and deep-fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain on paper.  
2. Warm carrot purée with kefir, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Steep yarrow in 50 ml hot water for 5 min, strain, cool slightly, and blend with lecithin to form a stable foam.  
4. On chilled plates, fan one leaf lace, scatter carrot-kefir gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of yarrow-flower foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Oyster Mushroom Stem Lace with Yuzu–Pear Gel and Fennel Pollen Foam

Ingredients:
- Oyster mushroom stems (from 8 mushrooms), cleaned
- 2 Tbsp tapioca starch
- Neutral oil for frying
- 100 ml pure pear juice
- Zest and juice of 1 yuzu
- 1 g agar-agar
- 50 ml whole milk
- 1 tsp fennel pollen
- ½ tsp soy lecithin
- Pinch fine salt

Method:
1. Toss mushroom stems in tapioca starch, shake off excess. Heat oil to 170 °C and fry stems in small bundles until lace-crisp (≈1 min). Drain and cool.
2. In a small saucepan, combine pear juice, yuzu juice and zest; bring to a gentle simmer, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved, pour into a shallow tray, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.
3. Warm milk with a pinch of salt, remove from heat, whisk in fennel pollen and lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.
4. To serve, fan a lace of mushroom stems on a chilled plate, scatter yuzu–pear gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of fennel pollen foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Nopal Lace with Chayote-Coconut Ceviche and Maqui Berry Mist  
Ingredients:  
• 2 young nopal cactus paddles  
• 1 small chayote, peeled and diced  
• 50 ml coconut milk  
• Juice of 1 lime  
• 1 Tbsp minced red onion  
• 1 tsp minced chile serrano  
• Salt  
• 1 Tbsp maqui berry powder  
• 50 ml water  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Neutral oil for frying  

Method:  
1. Char paddles over a gas flame until lightly blistered; thinly slice into lacy strips, season with salt, and fry briefly in hot oil until crisp. Drain on paper.  
2. Toss chayote with coconut milk, lime juice, red onion, serrano and salt; refrigerate.  
3. Whisk maqui powder with water, stir in lecithin, then aerate into a fine mist.  
4. On chilled plates, fan nopal lace, spoon ceviche in the center, and veil each with maqui berry mist. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Nasturtium Seed Pods with Honey-Mustard Gel and Marsh-Samphire Foam

Ingredients:
· 12 nasturtium seed pods, rinsed  
· ½ cup rice flour  
· ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
· Pinch fine sea salt  
· 50 ml Dijon mustard  
· 1 Tbsp runny honey  
· 1 g agar-agar  
· 100 ml marsh-samphire infusion (steep 10 g samphire in 100 ml water, strain)  
· ½ tsp soy lecithin  
· Neutral oil for frying  

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a thin batter; keep cold.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C, dip seed pods in batter, fry 1–2 min until crisp; drain.  
3. Simmer mustard, honey and agar-agar 1 min, pour into a shallow tray, chill and cut into small quenelles.  
4. Whisk lecithin into samphire infusion and aerate into a light foam.  
5. Arrange tempura pods on chilled plates, top each with a mustard-gel quenelle, and finish with a spoonful of marsh-samphire foam.

Recipe Title: Crisped Pomelo-Pith Spirals with Ginger-Turmeric Gel and Lemongrass Foam

Ingredients:
• White pomelo pith from 1 fruit, peeled into 3 mm ribbons  
• 2 Tbsp simple syrup (1:1 sugar:water)  
• Pinch fine salt  
• 150 ml water, 1 inch fresh ginger and 1 inch fresh turmeric, sliced  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml lemongrass infusion (1 stalk bruised, steeped)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Zest of 1 kaffir lime

Method:
1. Toss pomelo pith ribbons with syrup and salt; coil into spirals and dehydrate at 60 °C until crisp (≈2 hr).  
2. Simmer ginger-turmeric slices in 150 ml water 5 min, strain, return to pan, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min; pour thinly into a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool lemongrass infusion, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, arrange pomelo-pith spirals on chilled plates, scatter ginger-turmeric gel cubes inside, crown with lemongrass foam, and dust lightly with kaffir lime zest.

Recipe Title: Burdock-Root Crisps with Yuzu-Chive Caviar & Honey-Lavender Foam  
Ingredients:
• 1 medium burdock root, peeled  
• 1 Tbsp olive oil, pinch sea salt  
• 50 ml yuzu juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml neutral oil (chilled to 4 °C)  
• 2 Tbsp chopped chives  
• 1 Tbsp honey  
• 1 tsp dried culinary lavender  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 150 °C. Slice burdock into paper-thin ribbons, toss with oil and salt, bake 15–20 min until crisp; cool.  
2. In a saucepan, simmer yuzu juice and agar-agar for 2 min, strain and let cool to 40 °C. Drop spoonfuls into chilled oil to form firm “caviar” beads; rinse under cold water.  
3. Warm honey with lavender over low heat, steep 5 min, strain, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to create a stable foam.  
4. To serve, fan burdock crisps on a chilled plate, scatter yuzu-chive caviar, and crown with honey-lavender foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Coffee‐Leaf Lace with Avocado‐Lime Gelee, Cardamom‐Coconut Foam & Moringa‐Cocoa Soil

Ingredients:
• 8 large coffee leaves, patted dry  
• 1 ripe avocado, puréed  
• Zest and juice of 1 lime  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut cream  
• 4 green cardamom pods, crushed  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 1 Tbsp moringa powder  
• 2 Tbsp toasted cocoa nibs, ground  
• Neutral oil, tapioca starch, fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust coffee leaves with tapioca starch, fry at 170 °C until lace-crisp; drain on paper.  
2. In a saucepan, combine avocado purée, lime zest, juice and agar-agar; simmer 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut cream with crushed cardamom for 5 min, strain, cool, then whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. Mix moringa powder and ground cocoa nibs to create a soil.  
5. To serve, place a coffee-leaf lace on each chilled plate, scatter avocado-lime gel cubes atop, crown with cardamom-coconut foam, and finish with a dusting of moringa-cocoa soil.

Recipe Title: Charred Banana-Stem Ribbons with Papaya-Vanilla Gel and Hemp-Seed Soil

Ingredients:
• 1 banana stem core, peeled and spiralized into 3 mm ribbons  
• 200 g ripe papaya, puréed  
• 1 tsp vanilla extract  
• Pinch fine salt  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 2 Tbsp toasted hemp seeds, coarsely ground  
• 1 Tbsp honey  

Method:
1. Blanch banana-stem ribbons 1 min in boiling salted water, shock in ice, pat dry, then quickly char in a hot skillet until edges brown; set aside.  
2. In a small saucepan, warm papaya purée with vanilla and salt, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Toast hemp seeds in a dry skillet until fragrant; coarsely grind to a “soil.”  
4. To serve, fan charred ribbons on chilled plates, scatter papaya-vanilla gel cubes atop, drizzle with honey and finish with a sprinkling of hemp-seed soil.

Recipe Title: Charred Wood Ear Fungus Lace with Pea-Tendril Mousse and Toasted Hazelnut Crumble  
Ingredients:
20 g dried wood ear mushrooms (rehydrated, patted dry)  
½ cup fresh pea tendrils  
50 g ricotta  
1 tsp lemon juice  
Pinch fine sea salt  
1 tsp soy lecithin  
Neutral oil for frying  
2 Tbsp toasted hazelnuts, finely ground  

Method:
1. Heat oil to 170 °C. Fry small nests of wood ear until lacy-crisp (≈1 min); drain on paper.  
2. Purée pea tendrils, ricotta, lemon juice and salt; strain.  
3. Stir in lecithin and aerate into a light mousse.  
4. On chilled plates, place fungus laces, pipe pea-tendril mousse atop each, and finish with a dusting of hazelnut crumble. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Puffed Wild Rice Cups with Calamansi Gelee and Chicory-Root Foam

Ingredients:
- 50 g wild rice  
- Neutral oil for puffing  
- 150 ml calamansi juice  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 50 ml coconut milk  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- 1 tsp chicory-root powder  
- Fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Heat oil to 180 °C. In batches, add wild rice, cover, and pop for 20 s. Drain and, while warm, press into 3 small cup shapes.  
2. Simmer calamansi juice with agar-agar for 1 min. Pour as a thin layer in a tray, chill until firm, then cut into 4 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with a pinch of salt, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. Lightly dust the rim of each rice cup with chicory powder. Fill cups with calamansi gelee cubes and top with a spoonful of coconut-chicory foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Sichuan Pepper-Leaf Lace with Matcha-Mint Caviar and Cherry-Verbena Foam

Ingredients:
• 10 fresh Sichuan pepper leaves, patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml cherry juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 1 tsp matcha powder  
• 50 ml mint infusion (fresh mint steeped 5 min)  
• 100 ml verbena (lemon-verbena) infusion  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust leaves with tapioca starch and fry in oil at 170 °C until lace-crisp; drain.  
2. Simmer cherry juice with agar-agar 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into droplets (“caviar”) by pressing a fork.  
3. Whisk matcha into chilled mint infusion; heat gently, whisk in agar-agar, drop into ice-cold oil to form green “caviar,” rinse.  
4. Stir lecithin into room-temperature verbena infusion and aerate with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
5. Arrange pepper-leaf laces on plates, scatter alternating matcha and cherry caviar, and crown with spoonfuls of verbena foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Hosta-Petal Lace with Chokeberry-Lime Gel and Lovage Foam

Ingredients:
• 10 hosta petals, patted dry  
• 1 tsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral frying oil  
• 100 ml chokeberry (aronia) juice  
• Zest + juice of ½ lime  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml lovage leaf infusion  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly dust petals in starch and fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain.  
2. Simmer chokeberry juice with lime zest, juice and agar for 1 min; pour thinly, chill, then cube.  
3. Stir lecithin into cooled lovage infusion and aerate into foam.  
4. Fan hosta laces on a chilled plate, scatter gel cubes, crown with lovage foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Chanterelle Carpaccio with Rhubarb-Honey Air and Pistachio Dust

Ingredients:
- 100 g fresh chanterelle mushrooms, cleaned and sliced 2 mm thin  
- 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil  
- Pinch fine sea salt  
- 50 ml rhubarb juice  
- 2 tbsp honey  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- 2 tbsp toasted pistachios, finely ground  

Method:
1. Toss mushroom slices with olive oil and salt. In a hot dry skillet, sear 15 s per side until just charred; arrange on a chilled plate.  
2. Warm rhubarb juice and honey until simmering; remove from heat and whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to create a light air.  
3. Spoon a cloud of rhubarb-honey air over the carpaccio.  
4. Dust pistachio powder around the plate and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Chamomile-Steel-Cut Oat Crisp with Blueberry-Ginger Gel and Tarragon-Mint Foam

Ingredients:
• ½ cup steel-cut oats  
• 200 ml strong chamomile tea  
• 1 Tbsp honey  
• Pinch of fine salt  
• 100 ml blueberry juice  
• 1 tsp grated fresh ginger  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 3 fresh tarragon leaves  
• 5 fresh mint leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin

Method:
1. Soak oats in chamomile tea for 1 hr. Drain, toss with honey and salt, spread thin on a parchment-lined sheet, bake at 160 °C until golden-crisp (≈15 min); cool.  
2. In a saucepan, simmer blueberry juice with ginger 2 min, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm cream with tarragon and mint 5 min, strain out herbs, cool to room temperature, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve, arrange oat crisps on chilled plates, scatter blueberry-ginger gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of tarragon-mint foam.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Fennel Fronds with Nectarine–Sumac Glaze

Ingredients:
• A handful of fresh fennel fronds  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ¼ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 1 ripe nectarine, puréed  
• 1 tsp sumac  
• 1 tbsp honey  
• Pinch of sea salt  

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a thin tempura batter; keep chilled.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip fennel fronds into batter, fry 1 min until crisp, drain on paper.  
3. In a small pan, warm nectarine purée with honey and sumac just to a glaze consistency; cool slightly.  
4. Arrange fronds on a platter, lightly drizzle with nectarine–sumac glaze and serve immediately.

Pan-Seared Heart of Palm Steaks on Cactus-Flower Polenta Crisps with Pomegranate-Calamansi Foam

Ingredients:
• 2 hearts of palm, sliced 1 cm thick  
• ½ cup fine cornmeal  
• 1 cup vegetable stock  
• 20 small prickly-pear cactus flower petals, chopped  
• 50 ml pomegranate juice  
• Zest and juice of 1 calamansi (or lime)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Olive oil, fine sea salt

Method:
1. In a saucepan bring stock to a simmer, whisk in cornmeal and chopped petals. Cook until thick, spread in a thin layer on a tray, chill 1 hr, cut into 5 mm squares.  
2. Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a skillet, pan-sear polenta squares until crisp and golden; set aside.  
3. Pat hearts of palm dry, season with salt, sear 2 min per side until lightly browned.  
4. Warm pomegranate juice with calamansi juice and zest, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
5. To serve, place two polenta crisps per plate, top each with a heart-of-palm steak, and spoon pomegranate-calamansi foam over. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Cascara Chips with Lime Foam and Buckwheat Soil

Ingredients:
- 1 cup dried coffee cherry skins (cascara), patted dry  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- 2 Tbsp sugar  
- 50 ml fresh lime juice  
- Pinch of fine sea salt  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- 2 Tbsp toasted buckwheat groats, coarsely ground

Method:
1. Heat oil to 170 °C. Fry cascara skins in small batches for 1–2 min until crisp; drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. In a small saucepan, warm sugar with lime juice until dissolved; remove from heat and whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
3. Toast buckwheat groats in a dry skillet until golden, cool and grind coarsely.  
4. On chilled plates, arrange cascara chips, spoon a dollop of lime foam atop each, and finish with a dusting of buckwheat soil.  
Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Chocolate-Cosmos Petal Lace with Smoked Maple Foam and Pistachio Soil

Ingredients:
• 12 fresh chocolate-cosmos petals, patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil (for frying)  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 1 Tbsp pure maple syrup  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• 2 Tbsp toasted pistachios, finely ground  

Method:
1. Lightly dust petals in tapioca starch. Fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain on paper.  
2. Warm cream with maple syrup until just under simmer, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
3. Spread pistachio dust on chilled plates, arrange petal laces atop, crown with smoked maple foam, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Oyster Plant Leaf Lace with Pineapple–Black Pepper Gel and Borage Blossom Foam

Ingredients:
• 8 fresh oyster plant leaves (Mertensia maritima), patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml pineapple juice  
• ¼ tsp coarsely ground black pepper  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml borage flower infusion (steep 5 g dried blossoms in 50 ml water)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust leaves in tapioca starch and fry at 170 °C until lace-crisp; drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. Simmer pineapple juice with black pepper 2 min, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved, pour into a thin layer, chill 30 min, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool borage infusion to room temperature, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender into a stable foam.  
4. On a chilled plate, fan a leaf lace, scatter pineapple–pepper gel cubes over it, and crown with a spoonful of borage blossom foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Cauliflower Lace with Saffron-Orange Gel and Yuzu-Tarragon Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 1 small cauliflower, separated into thin “petals”  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 150 ml fresh orange juice  
• Pinch saffron threads  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 1 tsp yuzu juice  
• 1 Tbsp chopped fresh tarragon  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Lightly dust cauliflower “petals” in tapioca starch. Fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain and season.  
2. Warm orange juice with saffron, steep 5 min, strain. Whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into small cubes.  
3. Warm cream with yuzu juice and tarragon, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. On chilled plates, fan cauliflower lace, scatter saffron-orange gel cubes, and crown with a dollop of yuzu-tarragon foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Guava-Leaf Lace with Pineapple-Coconut Gel & Ginger-Basil Foam

Ingredients:
• 8 fresh guava leaves, washed and patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml pineapple juice  
• 50 ml coconut milk  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 1 tsp grated ginger  
• 5 basil leaves, torn  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly dust guava leaves with tapioca starch; fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp. Drain on paper, season with salt.  
2. In a saucepan, combine pineapple juice, coconut milk and ginger; bring to a simmer, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved. Pour thinly into a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool the gel slightly, stir in lecithin and basil, then aerate with an immersion blender into a stable foam.  
4. On chilled plates, fan guava-leaf laces, scatter pineapple-coconut-ginger gel cubes, and crown with basil foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Chive-Blossom Brittle with White Chocolate–Gooseberry Coulis and Lemon-Mint Foam  
Ingredients:
• 1 cup fresh chive blossoms, stems removed  
• ½ cup granulated sugar  
• 100 g gooseberry purée  
• 50 g white chocolate, finely chopped  
• 2 Tbsp fresh lemon juice  
• 1 Tbsp finely chopped mint leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Heat sugar in a dry saucepan over medium until it melts and turns deep amber. Working quickly, dip individual chive blossoms into the caramel, then chill on parchment until set.  
2. Warm gooseberry purée in a small pan, remove from heat, stir in white chocolate until melted and smooth; keep warm.  
3. Combine lemon juice, mint and lecithin in a bowl; whisk with an immersion blender until a light foam forms.  
4. To serve, arrange brittle blossoms on a chilled plate, drizzle with white chocolate–gooseberry coulis and spoon a tuft of lemon-mint foam atop each.

Recipe Title: Crispy Apple-Blossom Lace with Honeydew-Safflower Gel & Lemongrass-Citron Mist

Ingredients:
• 8 edible apple-tree blossoms, petals separated  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml honeydew melon purée  
• ½ tsp dried safflower petals  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml lemongrass infusion  
• Zest and juice of 1 citron (or lemon)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Dust petals lightly in tapioca starch; fry at 170 °C until lace-crisp; drain and season with salt.  
2. Blend honeydew purée with safflower; strain, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min; pour thinly, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Stir lecithin, citron zest and juice into lemongrass infusion; aerate into a fine mist.  
4. Fan blossom laces on chilled plates, scatter gel cubes atop, and veil with the lemongrass-citron mist.

Recipe Title: Popcorn-Nest Cups with Sunflower Petal Gel and Chamomile-Lime Foam

Ingredients:
- ½ cup popcorn kernels  
- 1 tbsp neutral oil  
- 100 ml sunflower-petal infusion (steep fresh edible sunflower petals in 100 ml hot water 10 min, strain)  
- 1 tsp sugar  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 100 ml chamomile tea  
- Zest and juice of 1 lime  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Heat oil in a pot, add kernels, cover and pop. While warm, press popped corn into four small “nests” on parchment; let cool.  
2. In a saucepan, warm sunflower infusion with sugar, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min. Pour into a thin layer on a tray, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Combine chamomile tea, lime zest and juice; whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a fine foam forms.  
4. Place two gel cubes in each popcorn nest, top with a spoonful of chamomile-lime foam, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura Tamarind Blossom Cups with Sweet Plantain Ribbon Nest, Passionfruit Gel & Coconut-Pandan Foam

Ingredients:
- 12 edible tamarind blossoms, rinsed
- 2 Tbsp rice flour
- ¼ cup ice-cold sparkling water
- Neutral oil for frying
- 1 large ripe plantain, peeled and spiralized into 1⁄8″ ribbons
- Pinch fine sea salt

For the Passionfruit Gel:
- 50 ml passionfruit juice
- 1 g agar-agar

For the Coconut-Pandan Foam:
- 100 ml coconut milk
- 1 tsp pandan extract
- ½ tsp soy lecithin

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour and sparkling water into a thin batter. Heat oil to 180 °C, dip each blossom, and fry 1 min until crisp cups form. Drain on paper.
2. In a nonstick skillet over medium heat, toss plantain ribbons with a pinch of salt until pliable, coil into small nests, and briefly pan-fry until edges golden. Cool.
3. Simmer passionfruit juice with agar-agar 1 min, pour into a shallow tray, chill until set (≈30 min), then cut into 5 mm cubes.
4. Warm coconut milk with pandan just below simmer, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until foam forms.
5. To serve, place a plantain nest per plate, nestle a tamarind blossom cup inside, scatter passionfruit gel cubes, and crown with coconut-pandan foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Kombu Lace with Mango-Lemongrass Gel and Pea-Mint Foam  
Ingredients:  
- 4 sheets dried kombu, rehydrated and patted dry  
- 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- 1 ripe mango  
- 50 ml lemongrass infusion  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 50 g fresh peas  
- 2 Tbsp mint infusion  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Lightly dust kombu in tapioca starch; fry at 170 °C until lace-crisp; season with salt.  
2. Char mango flesh under a broiler until blackened; purée with lemongrass infusion, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, chill and cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Blanch peas 1 min, shock in ice, purée with mint infusion, strain and whisk in lecithin to form a light foam.  
4. Arrange kombu laces on chilled plates, scatter mango-lemongrass gel cubes, crown with pea-mint foam, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Green Cabbage Lace with Gooseberry Gel and Gunpowder Tea Mist

Ingredients:
- 4 outer green cabbage leaves, trimmed and patted dry  
- 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- 100 ml fresh gooseberry juice  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 50 ml strong gunpowder green tea infusion  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Fine sea salt

Method:
1. Lightly dust cabbage leaves with tapioca starch, fry at 170 °C until lace-crisp (≈1 min), drain and season with salt.  
2. Simmer gooseberry juice with agar-agar 1 min, pour into a thin tray, chill until firm (≈30 min), then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Stir lecithin into cooled tea infusion, aerate with an immersion blender to form a fine mist.  
4. On chilled plates, fan cabbage laces, scatter gooseberry gel cubes, and veil each with gunpowder tea mist. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tapioca-Encased Pomegranate Arils with Avocado-Cilantro Vapor and Sumac Salt

Ingredients:
• 30 pomegranate arils  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 1 ripe avocado  
• 1 Tbsp lime juice  
• ¼ cup fresh cilantro leaves  
• 1 tsp soy lecithin  
• 1 tsp sumac  
• Pinch fine salt  

Method:
1. Whisk 1 Tbsp tapioca starch with just enough cold water to form a thin slurry. Dip each aril, then fry in 170 °C oil 20–30 s until a translucent shell forms. Drain on paper.  
2. Purée avocado, lime juice, cilantro and salt until smooth. Stir in lecithin and aerate with an immersion blender to create a light vapor.  
3. Arrange tapioca-encased arils on chilled plates, dust with sumac, then cloud each serving with avocado-cilantro vapor. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Arugula Blossom Cups with Green Strawberry Gelee and Garden-Cress Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 8 fresh arugula blossoms, stems trimmed  
• ½ cup fine semolina  
• ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml unripe (green) strawberry purée  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml garden cress infusion (steep 5 g fresh cress in 50 ml hot water, strain)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Whisk semolina, sparkling water and a pinch of salt into a thin batter; keep chilled.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip each blossom into batter, fry 1 min until crisp cups form; drain on paper and season.  
3. Simmer strawberry purée with agar-agar for 1 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
4. Stir lecithin into garden cress infusion and aerate with an immersion blender into a light foam.  
5. To serve, nestle a few gelee cubes into each crispy arugula blossom cup and crown with garden-cress foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Spiralized Cattail Shoot Spirals with Blood-Orange Gel and Tarragon-Lime Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 cup young cattail shoots (inner cores only), peeled and spiralized  
• Juice and zest of 2 blood oranges  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 5 g fresh tarragon leaves, torn  
• Zest and juice of 1 lime  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt

Method:
1. Blanch spiralized cattail shoots 30 s in lightly salted boiling water; plunge into ice water, drain, coil into spirals on chilled plates.  
2. In a small saucepan warm blood-orange juice and zest with agar-agar; simmer 1 min, pour into a thin tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Combine cream, tarragon, lime zest, juice and lecithin; blend with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. Scatter blood-orange gel cubes over cattail spirals, crown with tarragon-lime foam, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Dehydrated Sea Grape Clusters with Yuzu-Cilantro Gel and Coconut-Lime Foam

Ingredients:
• 8 clusters edible sea grapes (umibudo)  
• 100 ml yuzu juice  
• a small handful fresh cilantro leaves  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• zest and juice of 1 lime  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Rinse sea grapes, pat dry and dehydrate at 55 °C until just crisp (≈2 hr); reserve.  
2. Warm yuzu juice with cilantro 2 min, strain, whisk in agar until dissolved, simmer 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then dice into cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with lime zest, remove from heat, stir in lime juice and lecithin, then blend into a stable foam.  
4. To serve, arrange a few dehydrated sea-grape clusters on each plate, scatter yuzu-cilantro gel cubes and crown with a quenelle of coconut-lime foam.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Sweet Potato Leaves with Miso-Honey Drizzle and Hazelnut-Mint Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 12 young sweet potato leaves, stems trimmed  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 2 Tbsp white miso  
• 2 Tbsp honey  
• 100 ml hazelnut milk (blend 30 g soaked hazelnuts with water, strain)  
• 10 g fresh mint leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a thin batter; keep chilled.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip each leaf in batter, fry 1 min until crisp; drain on paper.  
3. Gently warm miso with honey until fluid; lightly brush over hot leaves.  
4. Steep mint in warm hazelnut milk 5 min, strain, stir in lecithin and blend to a stable foam.  
5. Arrange leaves on a chilled plate, crown with dollops of hazelnut-mint foam and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Trout-Skin Chips with Lingonberry Gel and Sorrel Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 4 trout fillet skins, scaled and patted dry  
• 120 ml lingonberry juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml fresh sorrel infusion (steep 5 g sorrel leaves in 50 ml hot water, strain)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• Fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Preheat oven to 150 °C. Lay trout skins skin-side down on parchment, season lightly, and bake until dry and crisp (~25 min). Tear into chip-sized pieces.  
2. Simmer lingonberry juice with agar-agar for 1 min, pour into a thin layer on a tray, chill until firm (~30 min), then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool sorrel infusion to room temp, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. Arrange trout-skin chips on chilled plates, scatter lingonberry gel cubes, and crown with sorrel foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Pineapple–Carrot Ribbon Carpaccio with Yuzu-Chive Foam and Wild-Rice Soil

Ingredients:
• 1/4 pineapple, peeled and sliced into 2 mm ribbons  
• 1 medium carrot, peeled and sliced into ribbons  
• 1 tbsp olive oil, pinch fine salt  

Yuzu-Chive Foam:
• 50 ml yuzu juice  
• 20 ml water  
• 1 tbsp chopped chives  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Wild-Rice Soil:
• 2 tbsp cooked wild rice, dried, toasted and coarsely ground  

Method:
1. Toss pineapple and carrot ribbons with olive oil and salt; char on a hot grill pan 30 s per side.  
2. Blend yuzu juice, water, chopped chives and lecithin; aerate into a light foam.  
3. Pulse toasted wild rice into a coarse “soil.”  
4. Fan ribbons on a chilled plate, spoon yuzu-chive foam atop and finish with a dusting of wild-rice soil.

Recipe Title: Crispy Black Trumpet Mushroom Lace with Chokecherry Gel and Peanut-Miso Foam

Ingredients:
- 8 black trumpet mushrooms, patted dry  
- 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- 100 ml chokecherry juice  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 50 ml smooth peanut butter  
- 1 tsp white miso  
- 50 ml water  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Pinch of fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Heat oil to 170 °C. Toss mushrooms in tapioca starch, fry in batches until lacy-crisp (≈1 min); drain and season.  
2. Simmer chokecherry juice with agar-agar 1 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm peanut butter, miso and water gently until fluid; remove from heat and whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, fan mushroom laces on chilled plates, scatter chokecherry gel cubes atop, and crown with a dollop of peanut-miso foam.

Recipe Title: Cricket-Flour Socca Crisp with Lime-Ginger Foam and Fennel-Pollen Dust  
Ingredients:  
• ½ cup chickpea flour  
• 2 Tbsp cricket flour  
• ½ tsp fine sea salt  
• ¾ cup water  
• 1 tsp olive oil  
• Zest and juice of 1 lime  
• 1 tsp grated fresh ginger  
• 50 ml water  
• ¼ tsp soy lecithin  
• 1 tsp fennel pollen  

Method:  
1. Whisk chickpea flour, cricket flour, salt, water and oil into a smooth batter; rest 30 min.  
2. Preheat oven to 200 °C. Spread batter paper-thin on an oiled baking sheet; bake until lacy-crisp, ~12 min.  
3. In a small saucepan, warm lime juice, zest, ginger and 50 ml water until hot; remove from heat and whisk in lecithin until foamy.  
4. Transfer socca crisps to plates, spoon lime-ginger foam atop each and finish with a dusting of fennel pollen.

Recipe Title: Sous-Vide Celery-Heart Terrine with Peach-Vanilla Gel and Tarragon Air  
Ingredients:  
• 4 celery hearts, trimmed  
• 1 ripe peach, puréed  
• Seeds of 1 vanilla bean  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 5 fresh tarragon leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Season celery hearts with salt, vacuum-seal and sous-vide at 85 °C for 1 hr. Press into a small terrine mold and chill until firm.  
2. Warm peach purée with vanilla seeds; whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill to set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm cream with tarragon leaves, steep 5 min, strain, then whisk in lecithin until a light air forms.  
4. Unmold and thinly slice the terrine. Fan slices on chilled plates, scatter peach-vanilla gel cubes, and crown with tarragon air. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Fermented Banana-Stem Spiral Carpaccio with Tamarind-Apple Gel and Coconut-Sage Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 1 small banana stem core, peeled and spiralized  
• 1 tsp sea salt  
• 1 tsp sugar  
• 50 ml tamarind concentrate  
• 50 ml apple juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• 5 fresh sage leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Toss banana-stem spirals with salt and sugar, submerge in 200 ml water, cover loosely and ferment at 20 °C for 24 hr. Rinse, drain and coil on chilled plates.  
2. Simmer tamarind concentrate and apple juice with agar-agar for 1 min, pour into a thin tray, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with sage leaves for 5 min, strain, cool slightly, then whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. Scatter tamarind-apple gel cubes over the banana-stem spirals and crown with coconut-sage foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Radicchio-Rib Lace with Blackberry–Balsamic Gel and Apple–Tarragon Foam

Ingredients:
• 6 large radicchio ribs, patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml blackberry juice  
• 1 Tbsp aged balsamic vinegar  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml fresh apple juice  
• 3 torn tarragon leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt

Method:
1. Lightly dust radicchio ribs in tapioca starch. Fry at 170 °C until lace-crispy (≈1 min); drain and season with salt.  
2. In a saucepan, bring blackberry juice, balsamic and agar-agar to a simmer; whisk 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Stir tarragon into apple juice, warm slightly, remove tarragon, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve, fan 2–3 radicchio laces per plate, scatter blackberry–balsamic gel cubes atop, and crown with dollops of apple–tarragon foam.

Recipe Title: Sorghum-Shiitake Waffles with Tamari-Tahini Drizzle and Quick-Pickled Kohlrabi Slaw  
Ingredients:  
• 1 cup sorghum flour  
• ½ cup all-purpose flour  
• 1 tsp baking powder  
• Pinch fine salt  
• 1 cup finely diced shiitake mushrooms  
• 2 large eggs  
• 1 cup milk  
• 2 tbsp melted butter  

For the drizzle:  
• 2 tbsp tamari  
• 1 tbsp tahini  
• 1 tsp honey  

For the slaw:  
• 1 cup thinly sliced kohlrabi  
• ¼ cup rice vinegar  
• 1 tsp sugar  
• Pinch fine salt  

Method:  
1. Preheat a waffle iron. In a bowl, whisk sorghum flour, all-purpose flour, baking powder and salt.  
2. In another bowl, beat eggs with milk and melted butter. Stir into dry mix, then fold in shiitake.  
3. Cook batter in the waffle iron until crisp and golden.  
4. Toss kohlrabi with vinegar, sugar and salt; let sit 15 min.  
5. Whisk tamari, tahini and honey into a smooth drizzle.  
6. Serve each waffle topped with pickled kohlrabi slaw and a generous tamari-tahini drizzle.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Bamboo Leaf Cups with Mulberry-Ginger Gel and Coriander-Lime Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 8 young edible bamboo leaves, cleaned & patted dry  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml red mulberry juice  
• 1 tsp grated fresh ginger  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml coriander-lime infusion (steep 1 Tbsp chopped cilantro and zest of 1 lime in 50 ml hot water, strain)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water & salt into a thin batter; keep chilled.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip bamboo leaves in batter, fry 1–2 min until crisp cups form; drain on paper.  
3. Simmer mulberry juice & ginger 2 min, whisk in agar-agar, pour thinly, chill until set (~30 min), cut into 5 mm cubes.  
4. Stir lecithin into coriander-lime infusion and aerate with an immersion blender into a light foam.  
5. Fill each leaf cup with mulberry-ginger gel cubes and top with a dollop of coriander-lime foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crisped Caper Leaf Lace with Yuzu-Honey Gel and Olive-Leaf Ash  
Ingredients:
• 12 fresh caper leaves, patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml yuzu juice  
• 2 Tbsp honey  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 2 Tbsp dried olive leaves (or black olives), charred and ground to ash  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust caper leaves with tapioca starch and fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. In a saucepan, warm yuzu juice and honey to a simmer, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, then pour into a thin layer; chill until set and cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Grind charred olive leaves into a fine ash.  
4. To serve, fan caper-leaf laces on a chilled plate, scatter yuzu-honey gel cubes over them, and finish with a dusting of olive-leaf ash.

Recipe Title: Fuchsia-Petal Carpaccio with Coconut-Mint Snow & Tamarind-Mustard Foam

Ingredients:
• 20 fresh fuchsia flower petals, washed and patted dry  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• 10 mint leaves  
• 1 tsp sugar  
• 1 tsp agar-agar  
• 2 tbsp tamarind paste  
• 1 tbsp Dijon mustard  
• 50 ml water  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Coconut-Mint Snow: Simmer coconut milk, mint and sugar 5 min. Strain, pour into a thin tray, freeze solid then grate into “snow.”  
2. Tamarind-Mustard Foam: Whisk tamarind paste and mustard into water with salt. Simmer 2 min, strain, cool to ~40 °C, whisk in lecithin until foam forms.  
3. To serve: Fan fuchsia petals on chilled plates, mound a spoonful of coconut-mint snow in the center, and crown with a dollop of tamarind-mustard foam.

Recipe Title: Toasted Breadfruit-Seed Lace with Soursop-Passionfruit Gel and Pandan-Peppermint Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 1 cup boiled breadfruit seeds, patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml soursop purée  
• 50 ml passionfruit juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• 1 tsp pandan extract  
• 5 fresh peppermint leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Blend seeds with starch to a paste, spread ultra-thin on a silicone mat, bake at 150 °C until lace-crisp; cool.  
2. Simmer soursop purée with passionfruit juice and agar-agar 1 min, pour into a shallow tray, chill, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with pandan and peppermint 5 min, strain, cool to 40 °C, whisk in lecithin into a stable foam.  
4. Fan breadfruit-seed lace on chilled plates, scatter gel cubes atop, and crown each with a spoonful of pandan-peppermint foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Rice-Bran Lace with Strawberry-Basil Gel & Lime-Yogurt Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 50 g rice bran  
• 2 Tbsp rice flour  
• pinch fine salt  
• 100 ml strawberry purée  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 5 basil leaves, chopped  
• 100 ml Greek yogurt  
• zest and juice of 1 lime  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Preheat oven to 150 °C. Whisk rice bran, rice flour, salt and just enough water into a very thin batter. Spread 1 mm layer on a parchment-lined sheet and bake 10–12 min until lacy-crisp; cool.  
2. In a small saucepan, simmer strawberry purée and chopped basil with agar-agar for 1 min; pour into a thin tray, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Whisk Greek yogurt, lime zest, juice and lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, fan a piece of rice-bran lace on a chilled plate, scatter strawberry-basil gel cubes atop and crown with a dollop of lime-yogurt foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Dulse Lace with Miso-Mango Gel and Lemon-Thyme Foam

Ingredients:
• 10 g dried dulse, rehydrated and patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 g ripe mango purée  
• 1 tsp white miso  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• Zest and juice of ½ lemon  
• 50 ml thyme infusion (steep 1 tsp fresh thyme in 50 ml hot water, strain)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly dust dulse in tapioca starch and fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain on paper.  
2. Warm mango purée with miso, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour thinly into a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Combine lemon zest, juice and cooled thyme infusion; whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve: fan dulse laces on chilled plates, scatter miso-mango gel cubes, and crown with a spoonful of lemon-thyme foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Rice-Paper Cups with Green Papaya-Passionfruit Gel and Kaffir Lime Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 4 round rice-paper sheets  
• 1 small green papaya, peeled and julienned  
• 60 ml passionfruit juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 2 kaffir-lime leaves, bruised  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• pinch fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Form cups: briefly soak each rice-paper in warm water, drape over an inverted small ramekin, then fry at 170 °C for 1 min until golden-crisp. Drain on paper.  
2. Make gel: simmer passionfruit juice with agar-agar 2 min, pour into a shallow tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Make foam: simmer coconut milk with bruised kaffir-lime leaves 5 min, discard leaves, cool slightly and whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. Assemble: fill each cup with papaya julienne, scatter passionfruit gel cubes on top, crown with a spoonful of kaffir-lime foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Corn-Silk Lace with Peony-Petal Gelee & Juniper-Honey Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 small bundle fresh corn silk, rinsed and patted dry  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 50 g edible peony petals  
• 100 ml water  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 2 tbsp honey  
• 1 tsp crushed juniper berries  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour and sparkling water into a thin batter. Heat oil to 180 °C, dip corn silk lightly, fry 30 s until lacy-crisp; drain and season with salt.  
2. Simmer peony petals in 100 ml water 5 min, strain, return liquid to heat, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a shallow tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Gently warm honey with juniper berries until fragrant, strain, cool to 40 °C, whisk in lecithin into a fine foam.  
4. To serve, arrange a corn-silk lace on each chilled plate, scatter peony-petal gelee cubes, and crown with a spoonful of juniper-honey foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Beet-Green Lace with Ginger-Pear Gel & Smoked Walnut-Oil Foam  
Ingredients: 8 fresh beet greens (washed, patted dry); 2 Tbsp tapioca starch; pinch fine salt; 100 ml pear juice; 1 tsp grated fresh ginger; 1 g agar-agar; 50 ml walnut oil; ½ tsp soy lecithin.  
Method: Lightly dust each beet green in tapioca starch, fry in neutral oil at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain and season with salt. In a small pot, simmer pear juice with ginger for 2 min, whisk in agar-agar until dissolved, pour thinly into a tray, chill until set and cut into 5 mm cubes. Warm walnut oil gently, strain, then whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to create a stable foam. To serve, fan one beet-green lace on each chilled plate, scatter ginger-pear gel cubes atop and crown with a spoonful of smoked walnut-oil foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Candied Nettle-Leaf Crisps with Persimmon–Rosemary Gel and Honeyed Green Tea Foam

Ingredients:
• 10 fresh nettle leaves (blanched 30 s, shocked)  
• 2 Tbsp honey + 1 Tbsp sugar  
• 1 ripe persimmon, puréed  
• ½ tsp finely chopped rosemary  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml strong green tea  
• 1 tsp honey  
• Pinch fine salt  

Method:
1. Toss blanched nettle leaves in honey and sugar; dehydrate at 60 °C until crisp.  
2. Simmer persimmon purée with rosemary and agar-agar for 2 min; pour thinly in a tray, chill, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm green tea with honey and salt; whisk vigorously to create a stable foam.  
4. To serve, arrange nettle crisps on a chilled plate, scatter persimmon–rosemary gel cubes, and spoon honeyed green tea foam atop.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Bitter Melon Blossoms with Honey-Ginger Glaze and Coconut-Pandan Foam

Ingredients:
- 8 fresh bitter melon blossoms, stems trimmed  
- ½ cup rice flour  
- ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
- Pinch fine sea salt  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- 2 tbsp honey  
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger  
- 2 tbsp water  
- 100 ml coconut milk  
- 1 tsp pandan extract  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a thin batter.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip blossoms lightly, fry 1 min until crisp; drain.  
3. Warm honey, ginger and water to a syrup; brush over hot blossoms.  
4. Heat coconut milk with pandan, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin into a stable foam.  
5. Serve blossoms drizzled with honey-ginger glaze, topped with coconut-pandan foam.

Recipe Title: Parsnip‐Skin Lace with Pear‐Ginger Gel and Lemon‐Thyme Foam

Ingredients:
- Skins from 2 parsnips, scrubbed and patted dry  
- 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- 100 ml pear juice  
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 50 ml lemon-thyme infusion (steep zest of 1 lemon and 2 sprigs thyme in 50 ml hot water, then strain)  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Pinch of fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lace: Lightly dust parsnip skins with tapioca starch. Fry in oil at 170 °C until lacy-crisp (≈1 min). Drain and season with salt.  
2. Gel: Simmer pear juice, ginger and agar-agar for 1 min. Pour into a shallow tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Foam: Combine lemon-thyme infusion and lecithin; aerate with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve: Fan a parsnip‐skin lace on a chilled plate, scatter pear-ginger gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of lemon-thyme foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Bee-Pollen Coated Goat Cheese Truffles with Lavender-Honey Foam

Ingredients:
• 150 g fresh goat cheese  
• 2 Tbsp mascarpone  
• 1 Tbsp honey (+ extra to taste)  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• 3 Tbsp bee pollen  
• 100 ml heavy cream  
• 1 tsp dried culinary lavender  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. In a bowl, blend goat cheese, mascarpone, 1 Tbsp honey and salt until smooth. Shape into 12 small balls; chill 30 min.  
2. Spread bee pollen on a plate; roll each truffle to coat evenly; return to chill.
