3. Gently warm cream with lavender and a little honey, steep 5 min, strain, cool to ~40 °C, then whisk in lecithin until foamy.  
4. Plate 3 truffles per dish, spoon a layer of lavender-honey foam over and around them, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tomato Caviar on Parmesan Tuile with Basil-Infused Olive Oil

Ingredients:
- 100 ml strained tomato juice  
- 2 g sodium alginate  
- 500 ml water  
- 5 g calcium lactate  
- 50 g finely grated Parmesan  
- 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil  
- 5 fresh basil leaves  
- Fine sea salt

Method:
1. Blend tomato juice with sodium alginate until smooth; rest 20 min to de-aerate.  
2. Dissolve calcium lactate in 500 ml water to make the setting bath. Using a pipette or teaspoon, drop tomato mixture into the bath; let spheres set 2 min, then rinse in clean water.  
3. Preheat oven to 200 °C. On a parchment-lined tray, make small 5 cm mounds of Parmesan; bake 6–8 min until golden and lacy; cool into crisp tuiles.  
4. Warm olive oil with basil leaves over low heat for 5 min; discard leaves and let oil cool.  
5. Arrange 6–8 tomato “caviar” beads on each Parmesan tuile, drizzle with basil oil, season lightly with sea salt, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crisped Sugarcane‐Rind Lace with Tamarind‐Tarragon Gel and Cardamom‐Coconut Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 cup sugarcane rind, peeled and sliced 2 mm thin  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml tamarind concentrate  
• 2 Tbsp chopped fresh tarragon  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• ½ tsp ground cardamom  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust sugarcane slices in tapioca starch; fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp. Drain and season with salt.  
2. Simmer tamarind concentrate, tarragon and agar-agar 2 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until firm, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with cardamom, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin to create a stable foam.  
4. To serve, fan sugarcane lace on chilled plates, scatter tamarind-tarragon gel cubes atop, and crown each with a spoonful of cardamom-coconut foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Moringa-Leaf Lace with Tamarind–Passionfruit Gel and Coconut–Saffron Foam

Ingredients:
- 20 fresh moringa leaves, washed and patted dry  
- 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- 100 ml passionfruit juice  
- 2 Tbsp tamarind concentrate  
- 1 g agar-agar  
- 100 ml coconut milk  
- Pinch saffron threads  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- Fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust moringa leaves in tapioca starch, fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain and season with salt.  
2. In a saucepan, simmer passionfruit juice, tamarind concentrate and agar-agar for 2 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with saffron for 5 min, strain, cool slightly and whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve, fan moringa-leaf lace on a chilled plate, scatter tamarind-passionfruit gel cubes atop and crown with coconut-saffron foam.

Recipe Title: Candied Sunflower Petal Lace with Almond-Miso Soil and Orange-Coriander Foam

Ingredients:
- 20 fresh edible sunflower petals
- 2 tbsp sugar
- 1 tbsp water
- 2 tbsp toasted almond meal
- 1 tsp white miso
- 100 ml fresh orange juice
- ½ tsp crushed coriander seeds
- ½ tsp soy lecithin

Method:
1. Heat sugar and water to a light simmer, stirring until dissolved. Briefly dip each sunflower petal, place on parchment, and let crystallize into crisp lacy shards.
2. Mix almond meal and miso into a loose “soil.”
3. Warm orange juice with coriander seeds, remove from heat, let cool to 40 °C, then whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to create a fine foam.
4. On chilled plates, fan candied petals, scatter almond-miso soil, and spoon orange-coriander foam around. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Chickweed Lace with Elderberry–Hibiscus Gel and Lemon-Balm Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 cup fresh chickweed leaves, patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral frying oil  
• 100 ml elderberry juice  
• 2 Tbsp dried hibiscus petals  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml lemon-balm infusion (steep 10 g leaves in 100 ml hot water, strain)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt

Method:
1. Lightly dust chickweed in tapioca starch and deep-fry at 170 °C until lacy and crisp; season with salt.  
2. Simmer elderberry juice with hibiscus and agar-agar for 2 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool lemon-balm infusion to room temperature, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, fan chickweed lace on chilled plates, scatter elderberry–hibiscus gel cubes atop, and crown each with a spoonful of lemon-balm foam.

Recipe Title: Coneflower-Petal Sorbet with Honeycrisp Apple Dust and Thyme-Honey Foam

Ingredients:
• 50 g fresh echinacea (coneflower) petals  
• 200 ml apple juice  
• 1 tbsp honey  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• 1 tsp agar-agar  
• 2 thin apple slices, dehydrated and ground into dust  
• 2 sprigs fresh thyme  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Blanch petals 10 s, shock in ice. Blend with juice, honey, salt and agar, strain into a shallow tray; chill until set. Scrape into sorbet with a fork.  
2. Warm thyme and a little honey 2 min; strain, cool to 40 °C and whisk in lecithin into a light foam.  
3. Spoon sorbet quenelles onto chilled plates, dust with apple powder and crown with thyme-honey foam.

Recipe Title: Sea Lettuce Lace with Celery-Apple Gel and Saffron-Chive Foam

Ingredients:
• 10 g dried sea lettuce (Ulva lactuca), rehydrated and patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml celery juice  
• 50 ml green apple juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• Pinch saffron threads  
• 1 Tbsp finely chopped chives  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lightly dust sea lettuce with tapioca starch. Fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp (≈1 min); drain and season with salt.  
2. In a saucepan, combine celery and apple juices with agar-agar. Bring to a simmer, whisk 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm cream with saffron threads, steep 5 min, strain, cool to 40 °C. Stir in chives and lecithin, then aerate with an immersion blender into a fine foam.  
4. To serve: fan lace on chilled plates, scatter celery-apple gel cubes atop, crown with saffron-chive foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred White Asparagus Carpaccio with Rhubarb-Mint Granita and Smoked Olive-Oil Foam

Ingredients:
- 6 white asparagus spears, peeled  
- 100 g rhubarb stalks, chopped  
- 2 Tbsp sugar  
- 1 Tbsp fresh mint, chopped  
- Pinch fine salt  
- 50 ml extra-virgin olive oil  
- ½ tsp smoked sea salt  
- 1 tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Preheat a grill or heavy pan. Snap off the woody ends of asparagus, brush with a little oil, char 2–3 min until lightly blackened. Slice thin on the bias and fan on chilled plates.  
2. In a small saucepan, combine rhubarb, sugar, chopped mint and a pinch of salt. Simmer gently until rhubarb collapses (≈5 min). Purée and strain. Pour into a shallow tray, freeze, scraping with a fork every 20 min to make a fluffy granita (~1 hr).  
3. Warm olive oil with smoked salt to just under simmer. Remove from heat, whisk in lecithin vigorously until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, mound a spoonful of rhubarb-mint granita atop the asparagus carpaccio and crown with a quenelle of smoked olive-oil foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Coral Lettuce Lace with Heirloom Tomato Water Caviar and Thai Basil Mist

Ingredients:
• 6 coral lettuce leaves, patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 200 ml heirloom tomato water (from finely puréed, strained tomatoes)  
• 1.5 g sodium alginate  
• 500 ml water + 2 g calcium lactate (setting bath)  
• 50 ml Thai basil infusion (steep 5 g fresh basil in 50 ml water, strain)  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt

Method:
1. Lightly dust leaves with tapioca starch and fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain and season.  
2. Blend tomato water with alginate until smooth; rest 10 min. Drop by teaspoon into calcium bath; let set 2 min, rinse in clean water to yield “caviar.”  
3. Whisk lecithin into basil infusion with an immersion blender to form a fine mist.  
4. On chilled plates, fan lettuce lace, scatter tomato caviar atop, and veil each with basil mist. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Sunflower-Seed Tortillas with Pickled Purslane Ribbons and Lime-Verbena Yogurt

Ingredients:
• 1 cup raw sunflower seeds  
• 3 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• 1 cup purslane leaves and stems, washed  
• Juice and zest of 1 lime  
• 1 Tbsp rice vinegar  
• 100 g Greek yogurt  
• 1 Tbsp finely chopped lemon-verbena leaves  

Method:
1. In a blender, combine sunflower seeds, tapioca starch, salt and just enough water (2–3 Tbsp) to form a pourable batter.  
2. Heat a nonstick skillet over medium, brush lightly with oil. Pour 2 Tbsp batter into 8 cm rounds and cook 2 min per side until golden and crisp. Cool on paper.  
3. Toss purslane with lime juice, zest and vinegar; let marinate 15 min.  
4. Stir verbena into yogurt.  
5. To serve, spread a thin layer of lime-verbena yogurt on each tortilla, top with purslane ribbons and a little extra lime zest.

Recipe Title: Buddha’s Hand Lace with Cashew-Mango Gel and Earl Grey Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 thumb-sized strip of Buddha’s Hand zest, patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp arrowroot starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 g fresh mango purée  
• 2 Tbsp cashew butter  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml strong Earl Grey tea, cooled to 40 °C  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Lace: Lightly dust Buddha’s Hand zest in arrowroot starch. Fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp, then drain and season with salt.  
2. Gel: In a saucepan, simmer mango purée, cashew butter and agar-agar for 1 min. Pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Foam: Whisk soy lecithin into the cooled Earl Grey tea with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve: Fan the citrus lace on a chilled plate, scatter cashew-mango gel cubes atop and crown with a spoonful of Earl Grey foam.

Recipe Title: Puffed Lentil-Sprout Cups with Date–Pomegranate Gel and Rosewater–Saffron Foam  
Ingredients:
• 100 g green lentils, sprouted 48 hr and patted dry  
• neutral oil for puffing  
• 100 ml pomegranate juice  
• 2 Tbsp date syrup  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml heavy cream  
• 1 Tbsp rosewater  
• pinch saffron threads  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Heat oil to 180 °C. Fry small nests of lentil sprouts 20 s until puffed; drain and shape into cups.  
2. Simmer pomegranate juice, date syrup and agar-agar 2 min, pour thinly, chill to set, then dice into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm cream with rosewater and saffron 5 min, strain, cool to 40 °C, whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam.  
4. On chilled plates, nestle lentil-sprout cups, scatter date–pomegranate gel inside each, and crown with rosewater–saffron foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Coffee-Rubbed Sweet Potato Medallions with Dark Chocolate-Sage Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 large sweet potato, peeled and sliced 5 mm thick  
• 1 Tbsp finely ground espresso  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 30 g 70 % dark chocolate, chopped  
• 2 fresh sage leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Toss sweet-potato slices with coffee and salt. In a hot skillet or over a grill, char 2 min per side until crisp-tender.  
2. Warm cream and sage leaves just below a simmer; remove leaves, stir in chocolate until smooth, cool to ~40 °C, then whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a light, stable foam forms.  
3. Arrange 3 coffee-rubbed medallions on each chilled plate and spoon the dark chocolate-sage foam over them. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Romanesco Rosettes with Lime-Basil Gel and Pumpkin-Seed Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 1 small Romanesco cauliflower, cut into 12 mini “rosettes”  
• 100 ml fresh lime juice  
• 10 g fresh basil leaves  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 g roasted pumpkin seeds  
• 100 ml water  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch smoked salt  

Method:  
1. In a hot skillet, char Romanesco rosettes 2 min per side until tender-crisp.  
2. Simmer lime juice with chopped basil 2 min, whisk in agar until dissolved, pour as a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Purée pumpkin seeds with water, strain, season with smoked salt, warm gently and whisk in lecithin to form a light foam.  
4. To serve, fan 3 rosettes per plate, scatter lime-basil gel cubes over them, and crown with a spoonful of pumpkin-seed foam.

Recipe Title: Peanut‐Skin Lace with Mango‐Chili Gel and Basil‐Smoke Foam  
Ingredients:  
• Peanut skins (from 100 g roasted peanuts)  
• 100 ml ripe mango purée  
• 1 tsp chili flakes  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 5 fresh basil leaves  
• 50 ml neutral oil  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Separate peanut skins after roasting, pat dry, dust lightly with tapioca starch, then fry in oil at 170 °C until lacy-crisp. Drain and cool.  
2. In a saucepan, simmer mango purée with chili flakes and agar-agar for 1 min. Pour ultra-thin on a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Char basil leaves over flame, steep in warm oil 5 min, strain, cool to 40 °C and whisk with lecithin into a stable foam.  
4. To serve: fan a piece of peanut-skin lace on a chilled plate, scatter mango-chili gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of basil-smoke foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Charred Celtuce Ribbon Carpaccio with Yuzu-Kosho Foam

Ingredients:
- 1 celtuce stem, peeled and thinly sliced into 1 mm ribbons  
- Zest and juice of 1 Meyer lemon  
- 1 tsp sugar  
- Pinch fine sea salt  
- 1 tbsp neutral oil  
- 1 tbsp yuzu juice  
- Pinch yuzu kosho  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Toss celtuce ribbons with lemon juice, sugar and salt; marinate 10 min.  
2. Heat oil in a pan and sear ribbons 30 s per side; arrange on a chilled plate.  
3. Blend yuzu juice, yuzu kosho and 20 ml water; strain, whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. Spoon foam over carpaccio and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Enoki Lace with Blood-Peach–Celery-Seed Gel and Marjoram–Yuzu Foam

Ingredients:
• 100 g enoki mushrooms, trimmed and patted dry  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• Pinch of fine sea salt  
• 150 g ripe blood peach purée (peeled, blended)  
• 1 tsp crushed celery seeds  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml yuzu juice  
• 5 g fresh marjoram leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Heat oil to 170 °C. Fry small bundles of enoki until lace-crisp (≈1 min); drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. In a saucepan, simmer peach purée with celery seeds and agar-agar for 2 min; pour into a thin layer on a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm yuzu juice with marjoram leaves for 3 min, strain out herbs, cool to 40 °C, then whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve, place an enoki lace on a chilled plate, scatter peach–celery gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of marjoram–yuzu foam.

Recipe Title: Elderflower Cotton Candy Nest with Goat-Cheese Lavender Mousse & Lemon-Thyme Dust

Ingredients:
• 100 ml elderflower cordial  
• 200 g granulated sugar  
• 100 g fresh goat cheese  
• 2 Tbsp heavy cream  
• 1 tsp dried lavender buds  
• Zest of 1 lemon  
• 1 tsp dried thyme, finely ground  
• Pinch of fine sea salt  

Method:
1. Candy Base: Warm elderflower cordial and sugar to 115 °C; spin in a cotton-candy machine to form delicate nests.  
2. Mousse: Blend goat cheese, cream, lavender and salt until silky; chill and pipe into small quenelles.  
3. Dust: Mix lemon zest with ground thyme.  
4. Plating: Center each cotton-candy nest on a chilled plate, top with a lavender mousse quenelle, and finish with a light dusting of lemon-thyme powder. Serve immediately.

Ingredients:
- 6 fresh eggplant blossoms, stems trimmed
- 100 g ricotta
- 1 Tbsp chopped parsley
- Fine sea salt
- 2 Tbsp olive oil
- 100 ml rhubarb juice
- 1 Tbsp honey
- ½ g agar-agar
- ½ tsp soy lecithin

Method:
1. Gently open each blossom, combine ricotta, parsley and a pinch of salt, and pipe into the blossoms.
2. Heat oil in a skillet over medium, sear filled blossoms 30 s per side until golden; transfer to a platter.
3. In a small saucepan, simmer rhubarb juice with honey and agar-agar 2 min; pour into a shallow tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.
4. Warm a few cubes back to liquid (≈40 °C), whisk in lecithin to form a light foam.
5. Scatter rhubarb cubes over blossoms, spoon rhubarb foam atop, and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Candied Orange-Peel Cups with Avocado-Yuzu Gel and Chamomile-Honey Foam  
Ingredients:  
• Peels of 2 navel oranges, blanched  
• 1 ripe avocado  
• 1 Tbsp yuzu juice  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml strong chamomile tea  
• 1 tsp honey  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch of salt  

Method:  
1. Blanch peels 2 min, pat dry, shape into small cups on a tray and dehydrate or bake at 120 °C until crisp.  
2. In a saucepan, mash avocado with yuzu, salt and agar-agar; simmer 1 min, pour thinly in a tray, chill and cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Steep chamomile in tea 5 min, strain, stir in honey, whisk in lecithin into a stable foam.  
4. Fill each orange-peel cup with avocado-yuzu gel cubes and top with a dollop of chamomile-honey foam.

Recipe Title: Lotus‐Seed & Black‐Rice Tempeh Steaks with Scorched Pineapple Gastrique and Shiso Oil  
Ingredients:  
• 1 cup cooked lotus seeds  
• ½ cup cooked black rice  
• ¼ tsp tempeh starter  
• 1 Tbsp rice malt or sugar  
• 4 pineapple rings  
• 2 Tbsp rice vinegar  
• 1 tsp sugar  
• 10 fresh shiso leaves  
• 4 Tbsp neutral oil  
Method:  
1. Blend lotus seeds, black rice, rice malt and tempeh starter; transfer to a perforated container and ferment at 30 °C for 24 hr into a firm cake.  
2. Slice cake into 6 mm “steaks” and pan-sear until golden.  
3. Char pineapple rings on both sides, purée with vinegar and 1 tsp sugar until glossy.  
4. Warm oil with torn shiso leaves for 5 min, strain to yield a bright green shiso oil.  
5. To serve, display tempeh steaks, spoon scorched pineapple gastrique over them and finish with a drizzle of shiso oil.

Tempura-Fried Magnolia Petals with Yuzu-Honey Foam and Pistachio-Matcha Dust  
Ingredients:  
• 12 fresh magnolia petals, rinsed and patted dry  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ¼ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 50 ml yuzu juice  
• 1 Tbsp honey  
• ¼ tsp soy lecithin  
• 2 Tbsp toasted pistachios, finely ground  
• 1 tsp matcha powder  

Method:  
1. Batter: Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt until just combined.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip each petal in batter, shake off excess, fry 20–30 s until translucent-crispy; drain on paper.  
3. Foam: Warm yuzu juice with honey until just under simmer, cool to 40 °C, whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. Dust: Stir matcha into ground pistachios.  
5. To serve: Arrange petals on a chilled plate, crown with a spoonful of yuzu-honey foam and finish with a sprinkling of pistachio-matcha dust.

Recipe Title: Pan-Seared Purple Sweet Potato Rounds with Yuzu-Cocoa Butter Glaze and Toasted Macadamia Crumble

Ingredients:
• 1 medium purple sweet potato, peeled and sliced into 8 mm rounds  
• 2 Tbsp cocoa butter, melted  
• 2 Tbsp yuzu juice  
• 1 Tbsp sugar  
• 3 Tbsp roasted macadamia nuts, finely chopped  
• Pinch of sea salt  
• 1 Tbsp neutral oil  

Method:
1. Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium. Season sweet potato rounds with salt and sear 3 min per side until tender-crispy; transfer to a warm plate.  
2. In a small saucepan, whisk cocoa butter, yuzu juice and sugar over low heat until just warmed and glossy.  
3. Sprinkle macadamia nuts in the now-empty skillet and toast 1–2 min until fragrant; remove from heat.  
4. Arrange sweet potato rounds in a single layer, brush with the yuzu-cocoa butter glaze, and finish with a scattering of toasted macadamia crumble. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Sunchoke-Peel Lace with Grapefruit-Rosemary Gel and Black-Pepper Foam

Ingredients:
• Peels from 4 Jerusalem artichokes (sunchokes), scrubbed and patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil (for frying)  
• Fine sea salt  

Grapefruit-Rosemary Gel:
• 100 ml pink grapefruit juice  
• 1 sprig fresh rosemary, finely chopped  
• 1 g agar-agar  

Black-Pepper Foam:
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Dust sunchoke peels lightly in tapioca starch. Heat oil to 170 °C and fry in small batches until lacy-crisp (≈1 min). Drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. For the gel: simmer grapefruit juice with rosemary and agar-agar for 2 min. Pour into a thin tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. For the foam: warm cream with black pepper just under a simmer, remove from heat, let cool to ~40 °C, then whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve: fan a piece of sunchoke-peel lace on each chilled plate, scatter grapefruit-rosemary gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of black-pepper foam.

Recipe Title: Baked Black Rice Crackers with Smoked Sherry-Vinegar Gel and Tarragon-Whisky Foam  
Ingredients:  
• ½ cup black rice, soaked overnight  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• 100 ml sherry vinegar  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml heavy cream  
• 2 Tbsp chopped fresh tarragon  
• 1 Tbsp whisky  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Drain the rice, spread into an ultra-thin layer on parchment, bake at 140 °C until fully crisp (≈20 min); cool and break into irregular crackers.  
2. In a small pot, warm the sherry vinegar with agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a thin tray, chill until set, then dice into 5 mm gel cubes.  
3. Warm cream with tarragon, steep 5 min, strain out herbs, whisk in whisky and lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, arrange crackers on a chilled plate, scatter sherry-vinegar gel cubes over them, and crown each with a spoonful of tarragon-whisky foam.

Recipe Title: Fermented Kelp-Noodle Spirals with Tamarind-Cashew Gel and Coconut-Lemongrass Foam

Ingredients:
• 100 g kelp noodles, rinsed  
• 1 tsp sea salt  
• 50 ml tamarind concentrate  
• 50 g raw cashews (soaked 2 hr, drained)  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Toss kelp noodles with salt, submerge in water and ferment 12 hr at 20 °C. Rinse, drain and coil into small spirals.  
2. Blend cashews to a paste. In a small pan, simmer paste with tamarind concentrate and agar-agar until dissolved. Pour thinly, chill until set, then dice into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with bruised lemongrass, steep 5 min, strain, cool slightly and whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve, fan kelp spirals on a chilled plate, scatter tamarind-cashew gel cubes over them and crown with coconut-lemongrass foam.

Recipe Title: Coffee-Maple Gel on Sweet Potato-Skin Lace with Cardamom-Coconut Foam

Ingredients:
• Skins from 2 sweet potatoes, patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml strong coffee  
• 2 Tbsp maple syrup  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• ½ tsp ground cardamom  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine salt

Method:
1. Toss potato skins in tapioca starch, fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain and season with salt.  
2. Simmer coffee, maple syrup and agar-agar for 1 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Warm coconut milk with cardamom, cool slightly, whisk in lecithin to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve, fan sweet potato-skin lace on chilled plates, scatter coffee-maple gel cubes atop and crown with cardamom-coconut foam.

Recipe Title: Pickled Wheatgrass Ribbon Salad with Coconut-Yuzu Foam and Black Sesame Soil  
Ingredients:
- 1 cup young wheatgrass shoots, cut into 5 cm ribbons  
- ½ cup rice vinegar  
- 1 tbsp coconut sugar  
- 1 tsp fine sea salt  
- 100 ml coconut milk  
- 1 tbsp yuzu juice  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  
- 2 tbsp black sesame seeds, toasted and coarsely ground  

Method:
1. Blanch wheatgrass ribbons 10 s in boiling water, shock in ice, then toss with vinegar, sugar and salt. Marinate 1 hr, then drain.  
2. Whisk coconut milk and yuzu juice, blend in lecithin with an immersion blender to create a stable foam.  
3. Grind toasted black sesame seeds into a coarse “soil.”  
4. To serve, arrange pickled wheatgrass ribbons on chilled plates, top with a dollop of coconut-yuzu foam, and sprinkle with black sesame soil.

Recipe Title: Charred Ice Plant Carpaccio with Peach Gelee and Nettle Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 12 ice plant leaves (Mesembryanthemum crystallinum), washed and patted dry  
• 1 ripe peach, puréed  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml fresh nettle infusion, cooled  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Lightly char ice plant leaves over a flame or in a hot skillet until edges just wilt; cool and slice paper-thin into a carpaccio.  
2. Warm peach purée with agar-agar until simmering, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Whisk lecithin into cooled nettle infusion with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. On a chilled plate, fan ice plant carpaccio, scatter peach gelee cubes over it, season with salt, and crown with a spoonful of nettle foam.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Wasabi Leaves with Quince Gel and Yuzu-Sage Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 12 fresh wasabi leaves  
• 50 g rice flour  
• 50 ml ice-cold sparkling water  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml quince purée  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml yuzu juice  
• 5 fresh sage leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a batter; keep chilled.  
2. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip leaves in batter and fry ~1 min until crisp; drain on paper.  
3. Simmer quince purée with agar-agar 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
4. Steep sage in warm yuzu juice 5 min, strain and whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender into a stable foam.  
5. On chilled plates, arrange fried leaves, scatter quince gel cubes atop, and crown with yuzu-sage foam.

Recipe Title: Roasted Lotus Root Chips with Yuzu-Ginger Gel and Watercress-Mint Foam

Ingredients:
• 1 medium lotus root, peeled and sliced 2 mm  
• 2 Tbsp olive oil  
• Pinch fine sea salt  
• 80 ml yuzu juice  
• 1 tsp grated fresh ginger  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 10 g watercress + 50 ml hot water  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Preheat oven to 200 °C. Toss lotus slices with oil and salt, roast 10–12 min until golden-crisp; cool.
2. In a small pot, simmer yuzu juice and ginger 2 min. Whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.
3. Steep watercress in 50 ml hot water 5 min, strain and cool. Whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.
4. On a chilled plate, arrange lotus chips, scatter yuzu-ginger gel cubes atop, and crown with watercress-mint foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Mustard Blossoms with Blood-Orange–Pepper Gel and Fennel-Seed Foam

Ingredients:
- 12 fresh mustard flowers, rinsed and patted dry  
- ½ cup rice flour  
- ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
- pinch fine sea salt  
- neutral oil for frying  

Blood-Orange–Pepper Gel:
- 100 ml blood-orange juice  
- zest of 1 blood orange  
- ½ tsp cracked black pepper  
- 1 g agar-agar  

Fennel-Seed Foam:
- 50 ml water  
- 1 tsp crushed fennel seeds, steeped 5 min and strained  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a thin batter. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip mustard flowers and fry 45 s–1 min until translucent-crispy; drain.  
2. Simmer blood-orange juice, zest, pepper and agar-agar 2 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Cool fennel infusion to room temperature and whisk in lecithin until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, arrange fried blossoms on chilled plates, scatter blood-orange–pepper gel cubes over them, and crown with a spoonful of fennel-seed foam.

Recipe Title: Charred Kudzu-Vine Lace with Lychee-Ginger Gelee and Osmanthus-Smoke Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 10 edible kudzu vine leaves, patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml lychee purée  
• 1 tsp grated ginger  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml osmanthus tea, cooled  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch of fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Lightly dust kudzu leaves in tapioca starch and fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; drain and season with salt.  
2. Simmer lychee purée with ginger and agar-agar for 2 min; pour into a thin layer, chill to set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Stir lecithin into cooled osmanthus tea and aerate with an immersion blender to form a smoky foam.  
4. To serve: fan one kudzu lace on a chilled plate, scatter lychee-ginger gelee cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of osmanthus-smoke foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Broccoli-Stalk Lace with Mango-Basil Gel and Coconut-Chili Foam

Ingredients:
1 large broccoli stalk, peeled into thin ribbons; 2 tbsp tapioca starch; neutral oil for frying; 150 ml ripe mango purée; 8 fresh basil leaves, chopped; 1 g agar-agar; 100 ml coconut milk; 1 tsp chili oil; ½ tsp soy lecithin; fine sea salt.

Method:
1. Lightly dust broccoli ribbons in tapioca starch, shake off excess. Fry in oil at 170 °C until lace-crisp (≈1 min), drain and season with salt.
2. In a saucepan, simmer mango purée with basil and agar-agar 2 min. Pour a thin layer into a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.
3. Warm coconut milk with chili oil just below a simmer. Remove from heat and whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.
4. To serve, fan broccoli-stalk lace on a chilled plate, scatter mango-basil gel cubes atop, and crown with coconut-chili foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Spirulina-Infused Tagliatelle Lace with Mango-Chili Gel and Cold-Brew Coffee Foam

Ingredients:
- 100 g fresh egg tagliatelle
- ½ tsp spirulina powder
- neutral oil for frying
- 100 ml mango purée
- 1 tsp crushed chili flakes
- 1 g agar-agar
- 100 ml cold-brew coffee
- 1 tsp honey
- ½ tsp soy lecithin
- fine sea salt

Method:
1. Toss tagliatelle with spirulina powder until evenly coated. Heat oil to 170 °C, fry small nests of tagliatelle until lace-crispy (≈1 min). Drain on paper and season lightly.  
2. Simmer mango purée with chili flakes, whisk in agar-agar, simmer 1 min, pour thinly into a tray, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Whisk cold-brew coffee and honey, then blend in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, fan one tagliatelle lace on a chilled plate, scatter mango-chili gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of coffee foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Crispy Yacon‐Skin Lace with Calamansi‐Sorrel Gel and Kumquat‐Thyme Foam

Ingredients:
- Skins from 2 yacon roots, scrubbed and patted dry  
- 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- Fine sea salt  

For the gel:
- 100 ml calamansi (or lime) juice  
- 8 fresh sorrel leaves  
- 1 g agar-agar  

For the foam:
- 50 ml freshly squeezed kumquat juice  
- 5 sprigs fresh thyme  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lace: Lightly dust yacon skins in tapioca starch, fry at 170 °C until lacy‐crisp (≈1 min), drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. Gel: Simmer sorrel leaves in calamansi juice for 2 min, strain out solids, whisk in agar-agar, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Foam: Steep thyme in kumquat juice for 5 min, strain, cool to 40 °C, whisk in lecithin, then aerate with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve: Fan one piece of yacon‐skin lace on each chilled plate, scatter calamansi‐sorrel gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of kumquat‐thyme foam.

Recipe Title: Fennel-Frond Crisps with Apricot-Juniper Gel and Tarragon Foam

Ingredients:
• 8 baby fennel fronds, washed and patted dry  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Apricot-Juniper Gel:
• 100 ml apricot nectar  
• 1 Tbsp crushed juniper berries  
• 1 g agar-agar  

Tarragon Foam:
• 100 ml heavy cream  
• 3 sprigs fresh tarragon  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Dust fronds lightly in tapioca starch. Heat oil to 170 °C and fry in batches until lace-crisp (≈1 min); drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. Gel: simmer apricot nectar with juniper and agar-agar for 2 min, strain, pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Foam: warm cream with tarragon sprigs, steep 5 min, strain, cool to 40 °C, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, fan fennel-frond crisps on chilled plates, scatter apricot-juniper gel cubes atop, and crown with a spoonful of tarragon foam.

Recipe Title: Potato-Starch Rösti Cups with Smoked Trout Mousse and Cucumber-Lime Foam  
Ingredients: 2 russet potatoes (peeled & grated), 2 Tbsp potato starch, pinch fine salt; 100 g smoked trout (skin removed), 50 g cream cheese, 1 Tbsp lemon juice; 100 ml cucumber juice, zest & juice of 1 lime, ½ tsp soy lecithin.  
Method: Preheat oven to 200 °C. Squeeze grated potatoes dry, toss with starch & salt, press into oiled mini-muffin tins and bake 20 min until golden; unmold. Purée trout, cream cheese & lemon juice until smooth and pipe into cups. Whisk cucumber juice, lime zest & juice with lecithin and aerate into a light foam. Top each trout-mousse cup with cucumber-lime foam and serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Jackfruit-Rind Cups with Turmeric-Mango Gel and Coconut-Lime Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 1 cup jackfruit rind (inner white skin), sliced into 3 mm strips  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Pinch fine salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml ripe mango purée  
• ½ tsp ground turmeric  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 100 ml coconut milk  
• Zest and juice of 1 lime  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:  
1. Batter and Fry: Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a thin batter; keep chilled. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip jackfruit-rind strips in batter, fry 1–2 min until crisp cups form; drain on paper.  
2. Turmeric-Mango Gel: Simmer mango purée with turmeric and agar-agar 1 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Coconut-Lime Foam: Warm coconut milk with lime zest and juice, remove from heat, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
To serve: Nestle two tempura cups per plate, fill with turmeric-mango gel cubes, and crown with coconut-lime foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Swiss-Chard Lace with Carrot-Turmeric Gel and Basil-Lime Foam

Ingredients:
• 6 rainbow Swiss-chard leaves (ribs removed)  
• 2 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Carrot-Turmeric Gel:
• 150 ml fresh carrot juice  
• ½ tsp ground turmeric  
• 1 g agar-agar  

Basil-Lime Foam:
• 50 ml lime juice  
• 20 g fresh basil leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly dust chard leaves with tapioca starch. Fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp, drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. In a small saucepan, simmer carrot juice, turmeric and agar-agar for 2 min. Pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Combine lime juice, basil and lecithin; aerate with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve: fan a chard lace on a chilled plate, scatter carrot-turmeric gel cubes atop, and crown with basil-lime foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Taro‐Leaf Lace with Coconut‐Lime Gel and Kaffir‐Mint Foam

Ingredients:
- 8 taro leaves, stems removed and patted dry  
- 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
- Neutral oil for frying  
- Pinch fine sea salt  

For the Coconut‐Lime Gel:
- 100 ml coconut milk  
- Zest and juice of 1 lime  
- 1 g agar-agar  

For the Kaffir-Mint Foam:
- 5 kaffir lime leaves, bruised  
- 50 ml hot water  
- ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Lightly dust taro leaves with tapioca starch. Heat oil to 170 °C, fry leaves in batches until lacy-crisp (≈1 min). Drain on paper and season with salt.  
2. In a small pot, simmer coconut milk with lime zest, juice and agar-agar for 2 min. Pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Steep kaffir leaves in hot water for 5 min, strain and cool. Whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, fan taro-leaf laces on chilled plates, scatter coconut-lime gel cubes atop, and crown with kaffir-mint foam. Serve immediately.

Recipe Title: Tempura-Fried Yucca Flower Cups with Camu-Camu Gel and Lemongrass-Mint Foam

Ingredients:
• 8 fresh yucca flowers, washed and patted dry  
• ½ cup rice flour  
• ½ cup ice-cold sparkling water  
• Pinch fine salt  
• Neutral oil for frying  

Camu-Camu Gel:
• 100 ml camu-camu juice (or frozen-thawed)  
• 1 g agar-agar  

Lemongrass-Mint Foam:
• 1 stalk lemongrass, bruised  
• 6 fresh mint leaves  
• 50 ml water  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  

Method:
1. Whisk rice flour, sparkling water and salt into a loose batter; keep chilled. Heat oil to 180 °C. Dip each flower, fry 45 s–1 min until crisp cups form; drain on paper.  
2. Simmer camu-camu juice with agar-agar 1 min; pour into a thin layer, chill until set, then cut into 5 mm cubes.  
3. Steep lemongrass and mint in 50 ml hot water 5 min; strain, cool to 40 °C, whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender until a stable foam forms.  
4. To serve, nestle two tempura yucca-flower cups per plate, fill with camu-camu gel cubes, and crown each with a spoonful of lemongrass-mint foam.

Recipe Title: Crispy Amaranth-Leaf Lace with Tamarind-Pineapple Gel and Ginger-Basil Foam  
Ingredients:  
• 10 fresh amaranth leaves, washed & patted dry  
• 1 Tbsp tapioca starch  
• Neutral oil for frying  
• 100 ml pineapple juice  
• 2 Tbsp tamarind concentrate  
• 1 g agar-agar  
• 50 ml water  
• 1 tsp grated ginger  
• 5 fresh basil leaves  
• ½ tsp soy lecithin  
• Pinch fine sea salt  

Method:  
1. Lightly dust amaranth leaves in tapioca starch; fry at 170 °C until lacy-crisp; season with salt.  
2. Simmer pineapple juice with tamarind and agar-agar for 2 min; pour thinly into a tray; chill until set; cut into small cubes.  
3. Steep ginger and basil in water for 5 min; strain; cool slightly; whisk in lecithin with an immersion blender to form a stable foam.  
4. To serve: fan one lace on a chilled plate, scatter tamarind-pineapple gel cubes atop, and crown with ginger-basil foam.

Give a proof for the Cauchy-Schwarz Ineq.answer:
Proof. Let a₁,…,aₙ and b₁,…,bₙ be real numbers and define for t∈ℝ the quadratic
  f(t)=∑ᵢ(aᵢ+t bᵢ)²
Since f(t)≥0 for all t, its discriminant must be non‐positive. Expanding,
  f(t)=(∑ᵢbᵢ²) t²+2(∑ᵢaᵢbᵢ) t+(∑ᵢaᵢ²),
so the discriminant D satisfies
  D=[2∑aᵢbᵢ]²−4(∑bᵢ²)(∑aᵢ²)≤0.
Hence
  (∑ᵢaᵢbᵢ)²≤(∑ᵢaᵢ²)(∑ᵢbᵢ²),
which is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

For real vectors a=(a₁,…,aₙ), b=(b₁,…,bₙ), one has the Lagrange identity
  (∑ᵢaᵢ²)(∑ᵢbᵢ²)−(∑ᵢaᵢbᵢ)²
  = ∑_{1≤i<j≤n}(aᵢbⱼ−aⱼbᵢ)².
Since each square on the right is ≥0, the left‐hand side is ≥0, i.e.
  (∑ᵢaᵢbᵢ)² ≤ (∑ᵢaᵢ²)(∑ᵢbᵢ²),
which is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

Proof. Let v and w be vectors in ℝⁿ. If w=0 the inequality is trivial. Otherwise set u = w/‖w‖, and decompose v = α u + v⊥ with ⟨v⊥,u⟩=0. Then
‖v‖² = α² + ‖v⊥‖² ≥ α², so |α| ≤ ‖v‖.
But ⟨v,w⟩ = ⟨α u + v⊥,‖w‖ u⟩ = α ‖w‖. Hence
|⟨v,w⟩| = |α| ‖w‖ ≤ ‖v‖ ‖w‖,
and squaring both sides yields the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

Let V be an inner‐product space and v,w∈V. Consider the 2×2 “Gram” matrix 
G = [⟨v,v⟩  ⟨v,w⟩; 
     ⟨w,v⟩  ⟨w,w⟩]. 
Because ⟨·,·⟩ is positive semidefinite, G must be positive semidefinite, so det G≥0.  Hence  
⟨v,v⟩⟨w,w⟩ − ⟨v,w⟩² ≥ 0  
which yields  
|⟨v,w⟩| ≤ ‖v‖ ‖w‖,  
the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

For any real numbers a₁,…,aₙ and b₁,…,bₙ, and any t>0, the elementary inequality 2|aᵢbᵢ| ≤ t aᵢ² + (1/t) bᵢ² holds term‐wise. Summing over i gives  
  2 |∑₁ⁿaᵢbᵢ| ≤ t ∑₁ⁿaᵢ² + (1/t) ∑₁ⁿbᵢ².  
Choose t = √(∑bᵢ²/∑aᵢ²) to minimize the right side, yielding  
  2 |∑aᵢbᵢ| ≤ 2 √(∑aᵢ² ∑bᵢ²),  
hence  
  |∑₁ⁿaᵢbᵢ| ≤ √(∑₁ⁿaᵢ² ∑₁ⁿbᵢ²),  
which is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

We prove by induction on the dimension n. For n=1, the statement |a₁b₁|≤√(a₁²)√(b₁²) is trivial. Assume the inequality holds for n–1. Write
S=∑_{i=1}^n a_i b_i = A + a_n b_n, 
U=∑_{i=1}^n a_i² = U' + a_n², 
V=∑_{i=1}^n b_i² = V' + b_n²,
where A=∑_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i b_i, U'=∑_{i=1}^{n-1}a_i², V'=∑_{i=1}^{n-1}b_i². By the inductive hypothesis A²≤U'V'.  Then
(U+ a_n²)(V+ b_n²) – S²
= (U'V' – A²) + a_n²V' + b_n²U' ≥ 0.
Hence S²≤UV, i.e. (∑a_ib_i)²≤(∑a_i²)(∑b_i²). This completes the induction and the proof of Cauchy–Schwarz.

Fix a nonzero vector b and consider the problem “maximize ⟨a,b⟩ subject to ⟨a,a⟩=1.”  Form the Lagrangian 
  L(a,λ)=⟨a,b⟩−λ(⟨a,a⟩−1).  
Stationarity ∇ₐL=0 gives b−2λa=0, so a=b/(2λ).  Imposing ⟨a,a⟩=1 yields 4λ²=⟨b,b⟩, hence |λ|=‖b‖/2 and the maximum of ⟨a,b⟩ is ‖b‖.  Thus for any a≠0,
  |⟨a,b⟩|=‖a‖·|⟨a/‖a‖,b⟩| ≤‖a‖·‖b‖,
which is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

Assume not all b₁,…,bₙ are zero (otherwise the inequality is trivial). Let B=∑_{i=1}ⁿbᵢ²>0 and define weights wᵢ=bᵢ²/B. For each i with bᵢ≠0 set yᵢ=aᵢ/bᵢ (and arbitrary yᵢ if bᵢ=0). Then
∑aᵢbᵢ=∑yᵢbᵢ²=B·∑wᵢyᵢ=B·E[y],  
∑aᵢ²=∑yᵢ²bᵢ²=B·E[y²].  
Since y↦y² is convex, Jensen’s inequality gives (E[y])²≤E[y²], so
(∑aᵢbᵢ)²=B²(E[y])²≤B²E[y²]=(∑bᵢ²)(∑aᵢ²),
which is the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.

Proof. In any inner‐product space V, fix v≠0 and define the linear functional f(w)=⟨v,w⟩. By the Riesz representation theorem, ∥f∥ equals ∥v∥, i.e.  
 ∥f∥=sup_{∥w∥=1}|⟨v,w⟩|=∥v∥.  
Hence for all w∈V,  
 |⟨v,w⟩|=|f(w)|≤∥f∥·∥w∥=∥v∥·∥w∥,  
and squaring yields  
 |⟨v,w⟩|²≤∥v∥²∥w∥²,  
the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality.
